title: Kīlauea Overlook — Hawaiʻi Volcanoes
description: Kīlauea is one of the world's most active volcanoes and the heart of Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park. This rim overlook faces Halemaʻumaʻu crater, where Pele traditions and modern eruption science meet. Steam plumes and occasional glow explain why this summit landscape is sacred and closely monitored.

title: Thurston Lava Tube (Nāhuku)
description: Nāhuku formed when a pahoehoe lava river crusted over and drained about 500 years ago. The short walk through rainforest into the tube shows how Kīlauea builds land from within. It remains one of the park's clearest windows into volcanic plumbing.

title: Chain of Craters Road Overlook
description: Chain of Craters Road drops thousands of feet from the summit area toward the ocean across decades of flows. Pullouts reveal pit craters, spatter cones, and highway segments buried by lava. It is a living record of the east rift zone remaking the Kaʻū coastline.

title: Mauna Loa Observatory Road Gate
description: This high road climbs Mauna Loa's north flank toward the NOAA observatory that has tracked atmospheric CO₂ since 1958. Thin air and vast lava fields explain the remote site choice. Upper graded sections favor high-clearance vehicles.

title: Punaluʻu Black Sand Beach
description: Punaluʻu's black sand is basalt pulverized by Kaʻū coast surf. Green and hawksbill turtles haul out on warm sand beneath palms. It is a classic circled-island stop and a reminder that new land here is only centuries old.

title: ʻAkaka Falls State Park
description: ʻAkaka Falls plunges 442 feet through Hāmākua rainforest northeast of Hilo. A paved loop also passes Kahuna Falls among ʻōhiʻa and tropical plantings. The park protects one of the Big Island's most photographed waterfalls.

title: Waipiʻo Valley Lookout
description: Waipiʻo — Valley of the Kings — was a political and spiritual center for early Hawaiian aliʻi. The lookout frames cliffs, black sand, and taro fields fed by ancient stream systems. The steep valley road is 4WD-only and often restricted.

title: Pololū Valley Lookout
description: At the end of Highway 270, Pololū opens as an amphitheater of cliffs and ironwood-lined black sand. Kohala is the Big Island's oldest volcano; these valleys predate Kīlauea's youth. The lookout starts a rugged coastal trail.

title: Puʻukoholā Heiau National Historic Site
description: Kamehameha I built this massive stone heiau in 1790–91 after a prophecy tied it to conquest of the islands. The temple overlooks Kawaihae Bay and ranks among Hawaiʻi's best-preserved royal heiau. It marks a turning point toward the unified kingdom.

title: Haleakalā Summit Visitor Area
description: Haleakalā — House of the Sun — tops 10,000 feet on Maui with a crater of cinder cones and āā lava. Tradition ties the summit to Maui snaring the sun; visitors still chase sunrise above the clouds. The road is one of the steepest paved climbs in the U.S.

title: Hosmer Grove Trailhead — Haleakalā
description: Hosmer Grove sits near the park entrance in a misty belt of experimental conifer plantings. Short trails introduce high-elevation flora and native forest birds. It is a quiet contrast to the stark summit crater above.

title: Kīpahulu — ʻOheʻo Gulch
description: At the far end of the Hāna Highway, ʻOheʻo pools cascade toward the sea through bamboo and rainforest. Kīpahulu was a productive coastal district for centuries; Pipiwai Trail climbs to Waimoku Falls. The remote road is part of the experience.

title: Waiʻānapanapa State Park
description: Waiʻānapanapa offers black sand, sea caves, a blowhole, and a coastal trail past cultural sites. Legends of Princess Popoʻalaea are tied to the freshwater caves inland. It is East Maui's signature stop before Hāna.

title: ʻIao Valley State Monument
description: ʻIao Needle rises above a West Maui stream valley where Kamehameha defeated Maui forces in the 1790 Battle of Kepaniwai. The park interprets the battle and botanical gardens along the walkway. It is a compact window into Maui's unification era.

title: Waimea Canyon Lookout
description: Waimea Canyon cuts ~10 miles long and ~3,000 feet deep into weathered Kauaʻi basalt — the Grand Canyon of the Pacific. Red walls and hanging valleys record millions of years of erosion on the island's oldest shield. Kōkeʻe Road pullouts deliver classic views.

title: Kalalau Lookout — Nā Pali
description: Kalalau Lookout peers into Nā Pali hanging valleys where cliffs plunge to the Pacific. Ancient Hawaiians farmed these isolated valleys, now reached mainly by the Kalalau Trail. Clouds often fill the amphitheater by midday.

title: Spouting Horn Park
description: Spouting Horn is a lava-tube blowhole on Kauaʻi's south shore that shoots spray with a deep moan. Nearby remnants recall 19th-century salt-making and shipping. It remains one of Poʻipū's most accessible geologic spectacles.

title: Puʻu o Kila Lookout — Kōkeʻe
description: Puʻu o Kila sits at the end of Kōkeʻe Road with views into Kalalau Valley and the Alakaʻi Plateau. Cooler upland forest sheltered ranching and later CCC-era park work. Trails explore some of Kauaʻi's last native forest stands.

title: Diamond Head (Lēʻahi) Trailhead
description: Lēʻahi is a tuff cone formed ~200,000 years ago and later fortified for Oʻahu coastal defense. The trail climbs through a military tunnel to a bunker-lined summit over Honolulu. It is both a volcanic landmark and early 20th-century Pacific strategy.

title: Nuʻuanu Pali Lookout
description: Here Kamehameha's forces drove Oʻahu warriors over the cliff in the 1795 Battle of Nuʻuanu, sealing the island's conquest. Trade winds roar through the pass year-round. The lookout sits beside the old Pali Highway with Windward vistas.

title: Pearl Harbor — USS Arizona Memorial Visitor
description: The visitor center anchors remembrance of the December 7, 1941 attack that brought the U.S. into World War II. The sunken USS Arizona still leaks oil beneath the white memorial. It is among the most visited historic sites in the Pacific.

title: Makapuʻu Point Lighthouse Trailhead
description: Makapuʻu's lighthouse has guided ships past Oʻahu's eastern tip since 1909. The paved trail offers whale-season vistas and views of Mānana Island. It is a short, high-reward walk on the windward edge.

title: Kaʻena Point Approach — Mokuleʻia
description: Kaʻena is Oʻahu's westernmost tip — dunes, tidepools, and albatross nesting habitat. Tradition places a leaping-off point for souls here. Unpaved coastal access demands care within the natural area reserve.

title: Haleʻiwa Harbor Historic Shore
description: Haleʻiwa grew as a plantation town and later the North Shore surf capital. The harbor and Anahulu bridge still show plantation-era bones beside surf culture. It is the gateway to Waimea, Pipeline, and winter swell season.

title: Waimea Bay Beach Park
description: Waimea Bay is famous for big-wave surfing and for the valley's cultural complex inland. Ancient Hawaiians settled the fertile valley; missionaries later mapped the coast. Calm summers invite swimming; winters showcase Pacific power.

title: Byodo-In Temple — Valley of the Temples
description: This Byodo-In replica (1968) commemorates a century of Japanese immigration to Hawaiʻi. Set against Koʻolau cliffs in Kāneʻohe, it mirrors the Uji temple in Japan. The grounds are a quiet Windward cultural stop.

title: Hanauma Bay Overlook
description: Hanauma is a volcanic tuff ring breached by the sea, now a marine life conservation district. The overlook frames the classic horseshoe bay above the parking area. Entry limits protect the reef that made it Oʻahu's iconic snorkel cove.

title: Hālona Blowhole Lookout
description: Hālona Blowhole forces surf through a lava tube in the coastal cliffs east of Hanauma. The lookout also frames Hālona Cove, filmed in From Here to Eternity. It is a quick geologic stop on Kalanianaʻole Highway.

title: Volcano House Historic Rim Area
description: Volcano House has hosted crater-rim travelers since the mid-1800s — among Hawaiʻi's oldest lodgings. Mark Twain and generations of scientists wrote from porches above Kīlauea. The rim complex continues that tradition inside the national park.

title: South Point (Ka Lae) Approach
description: Ka Lae is the southernmost point of the United States and a National Historic Landmark of early Polynesian landfall. Mooring holes and heiau remnants speak to centuries of fishing and navigation. Windswept cliffs feel like the edge of the map.

title: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area
description: Hāpuna ranks among the best white-sand beaches in the U.S., on the dry Kohala–Kona coast. Seasonal sands shift against resort and lava-field backdrops. It shows the Big Island's rain-shadow side opposite Hilo's wet coast.

title: Kealakekua Bay Overlook
description: Kealakekua Bay is where Captain Cook was killed in 1779 after first being received during makahiki. A white obelisk marks the far shore from Nāpōʻopoʻo. Steep cliffs frame one of Hawaiʻi's most consequential contact-history landscapes.

title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau (Place of Refuge)
description: This puʻuhonua offered sanctuary to kapu breakers and defeated warriors seeking absolution. Great walls, kiʻi, and Hale o Keawe face a quiet cove. It is among the best-preserved examples of traditional Hawaiian refuge law.

title: Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station
description: The VIS sits near 9,200 feet on Mauna Kea — sacred to Poliʻahu and home to world-class observatories. Ancient adze quarries and modern telescopes share the summit region. The road to the station is steep; beyond is 4WD and altitude-sensitive.

title: Lava Tree State Monument
description: Lava Tree preserves molds formed when 1790 pahoehoe surged through a wet ʻōhiʻa forest and chilled around trunks. The resulting stone 'trees' record a moment of Kīlauea's east rift history. A short loop explains the process in place.

title: Rainbow Falls (Waiānuenue)
description: Rainbow Falls drops into a large natural pool on the Wailuku River at Hilo's edge. Morning mist often throws rainbows across the basalt amphitheater. Legends of Hina and the river goddess are part of local interpretation.

title: Kaumana Caves County Park
description: Kaumana Caves are lava tubes from the 1881 Mauna Loa flow that once threatened Hilo. Skylights drop into cool, rough passages just above town. Bring lights — the tubes show how close historic eruptions came to the city.

title: Keōkea Beach Park — North Kohala
description: Keōkea sits on a rugged North Kohala cove near the Pololū end of the highway. Local families have used these shores for fishing and gathering for generations. It is a quieter coastal counterpoint to the busier Kohala resorts.

title: Lapakahi State Historical Park
description: Lapakahi preserves a partially restored fishing village along the Kohala coast. Stone house platforms and canoe sheds interpret pre-contact coastal life. The dry setting shows how Hawaiians thrived on the leeward shore.

title: ʻĀhihi-Kīnaʻu Natural Area Reserve Overlook
description: ʻĀhihi-Kīnaʻu protects some of Maui's last pristine coastal lava and coral ecosystems from the 1790 flow. Overlooks along Mākena Road frame raw black shoreline meeting clear water. Access rules prioritize reef and cultural site protection.

title: Hosmer's Twin — Hosmer Grove Camp Area
description: The camp area beside Hosmer Grove is a base for Haleakalā's misty forest belt. Early foresters tested timber species here; native bird habitat remains a focus. Cool nights and frequent fog define the mountain's mid-elevation mood.

title: Kalaupapa Overlook — Molokaʻi
description: From the pali overlook above Kalaupapa, cliffs drop nearly 2,000 feet to the isolation settlement peninsula. Hansen's disease patients were exiled here beginning in 1866; Father Damien and Mother Marianne Cope are central to its story. The view alone conveys the site's gravity.

title: Hālawa Valley Lookout — Molokaʻi
description: Hālawa is one of Molokaʻi's most storied valleys, with ancient taro loʻi and twin coastal waterfalls. Tsunami and cultural change reshaped settlement, but the amphitheater remains iconic. The lookout sits at the east end of Highway 450.

title: Puʻu Pehe (Sweetheart Rock) Overlook
description: Puʻu Pehe is a sea stack off Lānaʻi's Hulopoʻe–Mānele coast tied to a tragic love legend. Trails from Mānele offer views of the islet and marine preserve waters. It is Lānaʻi's signature coastal landmark.

title: Garden of the Gods (Keahiakawelo)
description: Keahiakawelo's red and orange rock sculptures sit on Lānaʻi's windswept uplands. Legends credit the forms to a contest of fire and wind between island priests. Dirt roads across the Palawai–Kanepuʻu area favor high clearance.

title: Exit Glacier — Kenai Fjords
description: Exit Glacier is one of the most accessible tidewater-region glaciers in Kenai Fjords National Park. Rapid retreat here has become a public timeline of climate change, with dated signs marking former ice edges. The valley walk shows raw moraine and outwash left behind.

title: Independence Mine State Historical Park
description: Independence Mine was a major hard-rock gold operation in the Hatcher Pass district above Palmer. Boardwalks and mill ruins interpret the 1930s–50s boom that drew miners into the Talkeetna Mountains. The alpine setting is as striking as the industrial archaeology.

title: Worthington Glacier Recreation Site
description: Worthington Glacier spills toward the Richardson Highway east of Thompson Pass. It is one of Alaska's roadside glaciers, with short trails to viewpoints over blue ice and debris bands. Thompson Pass itself is legendary for extreme snowfall.

title: Eagle River Nature Center Trailhead
description: The nature center anchors Chugach State Park access up Eagle River Valley near Anchorage. Trails interpret boreal forest, salmon streams, and occasional moose or bear sign. It is a classic urban-wildland gateway for Southcentral Alaska.

title: Turnagain Arm Beluga Point
description: Beluga Point overlooks Turnagain Arm's extreme tides and mudflats where belugas sometimes hunt. Captain Cook named the arm after having to 'turn again' in exploration. Bore tides and mountain walls make it a signature Seward Highway stop.

title: Portage Glacier Causeway Area
description: Portage Lake and the Begich, Boggs Visitor Center interpret a glacier that has retreated out of easy view since the mid-20th century. Icebergs still calve into the lake on boat tours. The corridor links Turnagain Arm to the Whittier tunnel approach.

title: Denali Viewpoint South — Parks Highway
description: Clear-day pullouts on the Parks Highway frame Denali, North America's highest peak at 20,310 feet. Athabascan peoples have long known the mountain as Denali — the High One. Roadside views here rival many in-park vistas when weather cooperates.

title: Savage River Check Station — Denali
description: Savage River marks the primary private-vehicle limit on the Denali Park Road. Beyond, buses protect wildlife viewing along a gravel corridor into the Alaska Range. The area mixes tundra, braided river, and classic Denali approaches.

title: Chena Hot Springs Road End Area
description: Chena Hot Springs has drawn Interior Alaska travelers for over a century to granite country northeast of Fairbanks. Natural mineral waters and aurora-season tourism define the modern resort. The long road in is a classic Interior overland spur.

title: Arctic Circle Wayside — Dalton Highway
description: This Dalton Highway wayside marks 66°33′N, where continuous daylight or darkness can occur. The haul road was built for the Trans-Alaska Pipeline in the 1970s. Reaching it is a badge of Interior and North Slope overlanding.

title: Finger Mountain Wayside — Dalton Hwy
description: Finger Mountain's granite tor rises above tundra along the Dalton south of the Arctic Circle. Pullouts interpret alpine-arctic botany and pipeline history. It is a landmark on the lonely haul to Deadhorse.

title: Keystone Canyon — Bridal Veil Falls
description: Keystone Canyon concentrates waterfalls and old railroad grade scars along the Richardson Highway near Valdez. Bridal Veil and Horsetail Falls drop from hanging valleys toward the canyon floor. It was a chokepoint for early copper and gold transport to the port.

title: Crow Creek Mine Road — Girdwood
description: Crow Creek was one of Southcentral Alaska's productive placer creeks during the Turnagain Arm gold rush. A historic mine site still offers panning demonstrations in summer. The dirt road climbs into Chugach forest above Girdwood.

title: Hatcher Pass Summit Lodge Area
description: Hatcher Pass links the Matanuska and Willow sides across alpine tundra and old mine roads. Gold history and modern backcountry skiing share the same ridges. Summer access is scenic; shoulder seasons can be snowed in quickly.

title: Norris Glacier Viewpoint — Juneau Icefield Area
description: Pullouts near Juneau frame arms of the Juneau Icefield, one of the largest icefields in North America. Tidewater and valley glaciers here feed iceberg-studded inlets. The capital's wild backyard is a defining Southeast Alaska landscape.

title: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center
description: Hurricane Ridge offers Olympic National Park's most accessible alpine meadows and views of the glacier-clad interior. The road climbs from Port Angeles through montane forest into wind-scoured ridges. It is the classic introduction to the Olympic rainshadow contrast.

title: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center
description: The Hoh is a temperate rainforest receiving well over 100 inches of rain a year. Maple and spruce drip with moss along the Hall of Mosses trails. It showcases why the Olympics host one of the world's great remaining temperate rainforests.

title: Cape Flattery Trailhead
description: Cape Flattery is the northwesternmost point of the contiguous U.S., on Makah lands. Boardwalks lead to cliffs overlooking Tatoosh Island and wild Pacific swells. Makah cultural history and treaty rights are central to understanding this cape.

title: Diablo Lake Overlook — North Cascades
description: Diablo Lake's turquoise color comes from glacial flour suspended in Skagit River hydro reservoir water. The overlook sits on the North Cascades Highway amid some of the most rugged peaks in the Lower 48. Dam history and wilderness aesthetics meet here.

title: Artist Point — Mount Baker
description: Artist Point is the end of the Mount Baker Highway with close views of Mount Baker and Mount Shuksan. The volcanic stratovolcano and jagged Shuksan ridges define Pacific Northwest postcard scenery. Snow often lingers into midsummer.

title: Maryhill Stonehenge Memorial
description: This full-scale Stonehenge replica overlooking the Columbia was built by Sam Hill as a World War I memorial. It opened in the 1920s as a reminder of the cost of war. The bluff setting also frames Columbia Gorge wind and river traffic.

title: Cape Disappointment Lighthouse Area
description: Cape Disappointment marks the mouth of the Columbia where Lewis and Clark reached the Pacific in 1805. Lighthouses and coastal defense batteries later guarded the bar known as the Graveyard of the Pacific. Cliffs and driftwood beaches complete a storied landfall.

title: Mount St. Helens — Johnston Ridge Observatory
description: Johnston Ridge faces the crater blasted open on May 18, 1980, named for volcanologist David Johnston. The observatory interprets the eruption that reshaped Spirit Lake and the Toutle drainage. Downed forests and pumice plains remain vivid decades later.

title: Beacon Rock State Park Trailhead
description: Beacon Rock is a volcanic plug rising beside the Columbia River, used as a landmark by Indigenous peoples and later by Lewis and Clark. A bolted trail climbs to a river-gorge panorama. Henry Biddle's early trail work preserved access for the public.

title: Palouse Falls State Park
description: Palouse Falls drops ~200 feet into a basalt canyon carved by Ice Age Missoula Floods. It is Washington's official state waterfall and a dramatic channeled-scablands landmark. Overlooks explain megaflood geology in plain view.

title: Salt Creek Recreation Area — Tongue Point
description: Salt Creek occupies a coastal WWII defense site west of Port Angeles with bunkers facing the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Tidepools and open beaches adjoin the historic batteries. It layers military history on Olympic Peninsula shoreline.

title: Multnomah Falls Historic Lodge Area
description: Multnomah Falls drops 620 feet in two tiers — Oregon's tallest and the Columbia Gorge's most visited waterfall. The 1925 lodge and Benson Bridge are Historic District contributors. Basalt cliffs record Columbia River Basalt Group flows.

title: Cape Perpetua Scenic Area
description: Cape Perpetua rises 800 feet above the surf with a Civilian Conservation Corps lookout heritage. Tidepools, Spouting Horn, and Devil's Churn show basalt meeting Pacific swell. It is a highlight of the Oregon Coast's public lands mosaic.

title: Crater Lake — Rim Village
description: Crater Lake fills the caldera of Mount Mazama after its catastrophic eruption ~7,700 years ago. Rim Village sits on the south rim above some of the world's clearest deep-blue water. Klamath traditions and scientific drilling both shape its modern story.

title: Smith Rock State Park — Misery Ridge TH
description: Smith Rock's welded tuff cliffs helped birth modern American sport climbing. The Crooked River bends below spires that draw climbers and hikers year-round. Ranching history and state park protection share the canyon.

title: John Day Fossil Beds — Painted Hills Unit
description: The Painted Hills display colorful claystone bands from ancient floodplains and volcanic ash. Fossils in the broader John Day formation rewrite Cenozoic mammal evolution in North America. Short trails protect fragile crusts while revealing the palette.

title: Hells Canyon Overlook — Imnaha Area
description: Hells Canyon is the deepest river gorge in North America, carved by the Snake between Oregon and Idaho. Overlooks frame ranch country dropping into wild river breaks. Nez Perce homeland and pioneer freight routes overlap in the canyon's story.

title: Fort Rock State Natural Area
description: Fort Rock is a tuff ring rising from Oregon's high desert, with nearby Fort Rock Cave yielding some of the oldest footwear in the world. The circular cliffs once stood in a pluvial lake. It is a landmark of Northern Great Basin prehistory.

title: Tamolitch Blue Pool Trailhead
description: Tamolitch — the Blue Pool — appears where the McKenzie River resurfaces after underground flow through lava. The striking turquoise pool sits in a dry waterfall amphitheater. Trails follow the McKenzie River National Recreation Trail corridor.

title: Silver City Ghost Town Approach
description: Silver City was an Owyhee Mountains silver boomtown with brick hotels and a long mining afterlife. Dirt roads across BLM and forest lands still reach a community of seasonal cabins and relics. It is Idaho's classic remote ghost-town drive.

title: Shoshone Falls Overlook
description: Shoshone Falls on the Snake River drops higher than Niagara in a basalt canyon at Twin Falls. Irrigation-era diversion and hydropower shaped modern Magic Valley agriculture. Overlooks explain why settlers called it the Niagara of the West.

title: Craters of the Moon — Loop Road
description: Craters of the Moon preserves a vast lava field on the Great Rift with cinder cones and tubes. Apollo astronauts trained here for lunar geology. The loop road samples pahoehoe, āā, and spaterry vents in a compact volcanic park.

title: Mesa Falls Scenic Byway Overlook
description: Upper and Lower Mesa Falls drop the Henrys Fork over rhyolite ledges on the Yellowstone Plateau's flank. CCC-era viewpoints frame one of Idaho's last unmodified large waterfalls on a major river. Lodgepole forest and basalt cliffs complete the scene.

title: Hells Canyon Dam Overlook Area
description: The road to Hells Canyon Dam follows the Snake into deeper canyon country below Oxbow. Dam building in the mid-20th century transformed river travel and power generation. Views emphasize the gorge's scale on the Idaho–Oregon line.

title: City of Rocks National Reserve
description: City of Rocks' granite domes guided California Trail emigrants who wrote axle grease graffiti on Register Rock. Today it is a premier climbing reserve with pioneer wagon traces. Silent City formations still look like a skyline of towers.

title: Glacier Point — Yosemite
description: Glacier Point overlooks Half Dome, Vernal and Nevada Falls, and the Yosemite Valley floor from 3,200 feet above. It became a carriage-road spectacle in the late 1800s and remains a defining Sierra viewpoint. Granite cliffs record ice-age sculpting of the range.

title: Olmsted Point — Tioga Road
description: Olmsted Point on Tioga Road offers a less-crowded angle on Half Dome and Tenaya Canyon's glacial polish. Named for landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted Jr., it sits in high Sierra lodgepole and slab country. Summer-only access follows snowmelt.

title: Bodie State Historic Park
description: Bodie is one of the West's best-preserved ghost towns, frozen in arrested decay after the gold boom faded. At ~8,400 feet east of the Sierra crest, winters are brutal and summers dusty. Streets of churches, saloons, and mills tell a raw boomtown story.

title: Alabama Hills Movie Road
description: Alabama Hills' rounded granite and orange metamorphic rock framed hundreds of Western films and timeless Lone Pine views of Mount Whitney. Movie Road loops past familiar formations used as celluloid stage sets. The BLM recreation area protects a cinematic landscape.

title: Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes
description: Mesquite Flat dunes rise from Death Valley's northern floor, formed by winds trapping sand near Grapevine Mountains. Star dunes and mesquite hummocks create a classic desert silhouette. They are among the park's most accessible dune fields.

title: Zabriskie Point — Death Valley
description: Zabriskie Point overlooks badlands of ancient Furnace Creek lakebeds eroded into golden waves. Named for a Borax company executive, it became a cultural icon in film and photography. Sunrise and sunset light make the soft hills glow.

title: Badwater Basin Salt Flats
description: Badwater Basin at 282 feet below sea level is the lowest point in North America. Salt polygons form as Death Valley's ephemeral lake evaporates. The stark flats explain the valley's name better than any plaque.

title: Keys View — Joshua Tree
description: Keys View overlooks the Coachella Valley, Salton Sea haze, and the San Andreas Fault corridor from the Little San Bernardino Mountains. On clear days the Peninsular Ranges stand sharp. It situates Joshua Tree National Park in active tectonic country.

title: Cholla Cactus Garden — Joshua Tree
description: A dense stand of jumping cholla thrives on a gently sloping bajada along Pinto Basin Road. The short accessible path shows how Sonoran and Mojave influences mix in the park. Golden hour turns the spines into backlit halos.

title: Torrey Pines Gliderport Overlook
description: Bluffs above Black's Beach host rare Torrey pines and a historic gliderport with Pacific panoramas. The reserve protects the mainland's rarest pine species against coastal development pressure. Hang gliders and migrating whales share the skyline.

title: Point Reyes Lighthouse Area
description: Point Reyes Lighthouse was built in 1870 on a windy tip notorious for fog and shipwrecks. Steps descend to the lantern room overlooking elephant seal beaches and open ocean. The peninsula's granite is an exotic terrane rafted north along the San Andreas.

title: Morro Rock — Morro Bay
description: Morro Rock is a 576-foot volcanic plug — the 'Gibraltar of the Pacific' — sacred to Chumash peoples and a navigational landmark for Spanish mariners. Quarrying scars remain from harbor work. Peregrine falcons nest on its cliffs.

title: Pfeiffer Beach Overlook Area
description: Pfeiffer Beach is known for purple sand from manganese garnet and Keyhole Arch glowing at sunset. It sits on Big Sur's wild coast where the Santa Lucia Mountains plunge into the Pacific. Access is a short Sycamore Canyon spur off Highway 1.

title: Bixby Creek Bridge Viewpoint
description: Bixby Creek Bridge (1932) is an Art Deco concrete arch that opened Big Sur to reliable auto travel. The viewpoint north of the span is among California's most photographed coastal scenes. Engineering and scenery made Highway 1 a world-famous drive.

title: Lassen Peak Trailhead Area
description: Lassen Peak erupted between 1914 and 1917 — one of the few Cascade volcanoes active in the 20th century contiguous U.S. The trailhead area interprets summit plugs and the Devastated Area. Hydrothermal basins nearby still hiss and boil.

title: Burney Falls — McArthur-Burney
description: Burney Falls drops ~129 feet as an unexpectedly wide curtain fed by underground springs as well as surface flow. Theodore Roosevelt reportedly called it one of America's wonders. Basalt cliffs and evergreen forest frame the mist.

title: Napa Sonoma State Historic Parks Hub — Sonoma Barracks
description: Sonoma Barracks and the plaza were central to Mexico's northern frontier and the short-lived 1846 Bear Flag Revolt. Adobe buildings still face the town square. The site anchors California's transition from Mexican Alta California to U.S. statehood.

title: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest Visitor Center
description: Schulman Grove protects Great Basin bristlecone pines among the oldest living organisms on Earth — some over 4,000 years. White Mountains geology and thin air shape their gnarled forms. The visitor center interprets dendrochronology that rewrote climate history.

title: Mono Lake South Tufa Area
description: Mono Lake's tufa towers formed underwater where freshwater springs met alkaline lake chemistry; falling levels exposed them. The lake is a critical migratory bird stop and a landmark of California water politics. South Tufa is the classic shoreline walk.

title: Valley of Fire — Elephant Rock Area
description: Valley of Fire's Aztec Sandstone blazes red among Mojave desert hills northeast of Las Vegas. Petroglyphs and Beehive-era CCC picnic areas share the park. Elephant Rock is a signature eroded arch formation near the east entrance.

title: Cathedral Gorge State Park
description: Cathedral Gorge's soft bentonite badlands erode into slot-like corridors and spires in Nevada's eastern desert. CCC structures and a slot canyon walk highlight Depression-era park building. It is a quiet geologic gem near Panaca.

title: Great Basin — Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive
description: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive climbs toward bristlecone pines and Nevada's second-highest summit inside Great Basin National Park. The road reveals classic Basin and Range topography — high peaks above dry valleys. Lehman Caves sit lower near the visitor center.

title: Sand Mountain Recreation Area
description: Sand Mountain is a singing dune complex beside Highway 50 — the Loneliest Road in America. OHV play and desert camping draw weekend crowds to the 600-foot dune. The sand sheet is a remnant of Ice Age Lake Lahontan shore processes.

title: Berlin-Ichthyosaur State Park
description: Berlin preserves a turn-of-the-century mining town beside world-class ichthyosaur fossils from an ancient inland sea. The combination of ghost town and Triassic marine reptiles is unique in the park system. Remote central Nevada roads set the mood.

title: Desert View Watchtower — Grand Canyon
description: Mary Colter's 1932 Desert View Watchtower blends Pueblo Revival architecture with one of the widest eastern Grand Canyon vistas. The Colorado River's bend and Painted Desert haze stretch for miles. It anchors the South Rim's east entrance story of tourism and Native design motifs.

title: Horseshoe Bend Overlook
description: Horseshoe Bend is a free-swinging meander of the Colorado River entrenched in Navajo Sandstone south of Page. The overlook became a global photo icon in the smartphone era. The river here sits downstream of Glen Canyon Dam inside Glen Canyon National Recreation Area.

title: Antelope Canyon X Area Approach
description: Upper and nearby Antelope Canyon slots were carved by flash floods through Navajo Sandstone on Navajo Nation land. Guided tours protect both the fragile corridors and cultural context. Beams of light in dust-filled chambers made the slots world-famous.

title: Monument Valley — Artist's Point Area
description: Monument Valley's buttes are icons of the Colorado Plateau and of Western film history on Navajo Nation land. Artist's Point frames Mittens and Merrick Butte in classic light. The valley remains a living cultural landscape, not just a movie set.

title: Canyon de Chelly — Spider Rock Overlook
description: Spider Rock rises ~800 feet in Canyon de Chelly, central to Diné (Navajo) stories of Spider Woman. Cliff dwellings of Ancestral Puebloans line the canyon walls below. Overlooks on the South Rim road interpret continuous Indigenous presence.

title: Sunset Crater Volcano Overlook
description: Sunset Crater erupted around 1085 CE, blanketing the area in cinders and reshaping Sinagua settlement patterns. The black lava fields contrast with painted desert hues nearby. A scenic loop links the volcano to Wupatki's pueblos.

title: Wupatki Pueblo Overlook
description: Wupatki was a multi-story pueblo that flourished after the Sunset Crater eruption enriched soils. Trade goods from the Pacific and Mesoamerica show far-reaching networks. The red sandstone complex sits between Flagstaff and the Little Colorado.

title: Montezuma Castle National Monument
description: Montezuma Castle is a cliff dwelling built by Sinagua people into a limestone alcove above Beaver Creek. Early settlers misnamed it; it has no link to Aztec emperors. The carefully plastered rooms remain one of Arizona's best-preserved Ancestral Puebloan sites.

title: Tuzigoot National Monument
description: Tuzigoot is a hilltop Sinagua pueblo overlooking the Verde River floodplain near Clarkdale. Dozens of rooms once housed a farming community tied to regional trade. The reconstructed walls help visualize Verde Valley life before Spanish contact.

title: Organ Pipe Cactus — Desert View Trail Area
description: Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument protects a Sonoran Desert landscape where organ pipe and saguaro mingle near the Mexican border. The scenic loop samples Ajo Mountain bajadas and bajada washes. It is a showcase of desert biodiversity in southwestern Arizona.

title: Sabino Canyon Visitor Center
description: Sabino Canyon cuts into the Santa Catalina Mountains on Tucson's edge, bringing water and cottonwoods into the Sonoran Desert. Tram roads and trails follow a canyon long used by Indigenous peoples and later by recreationists. Peak winter flow turns the desert briefly lush.

title: Kartchner Caverns State Park
description: Kartchner Caverns is a living limestone cave discovered in 1974 and opened carefully to protect formations. World-class speleothems grow in a humid underground world beneath the Whetstone Mountains. The park is a model of conservation-minded show-cave development.

title: Chiricahua National Monument — Echo Canyon
description: Chiricahua's rhyolite hoodoos — the Land of Standing-Up Rocks — formed from eroded volcanic tuff. Apache history and Faraway Ranch pioneer stories share the sky island. Trails wind through balanced rocks and narrow slots.

title: Four Corners Monument
description: Four Corners is the only point in the U.S. shared by four states — Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, and Utah — on Navajo and Ute Mountain Ute lands. The survey monument is a modern geopolitical curiosity on ancestral lands. Visitors typically stand in four states at once.

title: Goosenecks State Park
description: Goosenecks overlooks entrenched meanders of the San Juan River hundreds of feet below. The loops demonstrate how a river can cut downward while preserving its winding planform. It is a textbook Colorado Plateau viewpoint near Mexican Hat.

title: Moki Dugway Overlook
description: The Moki Dugway descends Cedar Mesa's cliffs on steep gravel switchbacks built for uranium ore trucks in the 1950s. Views stretch across Valley of the Gods toward Monument Valley. It remains a signature unpaved engineering scar on Utah 261.

title: Natural Bridges — Owachomo Bridge
description: Owachomo is the oldest and thinnest of three natural bridges carved by stream erosion under Cedar Mesa sandstone. Ancestral Puebloan sites dot the canyons. The park was Utah's first National Park Service unit.

title: Capitol Reef — Goosenecks Overlook
description: Capitol Reef protects the Waterpocket Fold, a nearly 100-mile wrinkle in the Earth's crust. Goosenecks Overlook peers into Sulphur Creek's tight bends. Pioneer orchards in Fruita add a human layer to the geology.

title: Goblin Valley State Park
description: Goblin Valley's Entrada Sandstone hoodoos resemble a crowd of mushroom-shaped goblins. The valley became a state park to protect the whimsical formations and nearby Wild Horse Butte views. Film crews and families share the sandy maze.

title: Kodachrome Basin State Park
description: Kodachrome Basin is named for the film that captured its colorful spires — sedimentary pipes that may record ancient springs or geysers. Red and white Entrada cliffs surround a quiet Grand Staircase valley. Trails weave among dozens of chimneys.

title: Calf Creek Falls Trailhead
description: Lower Calf Creek Falls drops 126 feet into a green oasis along the Escalante River corridor. Fremont pictographs and beaver wetlands share the canyon. The trailhead sits on Scenic Byway 12 between Boulder and Escalante.

title: Cedar Breaks National Monument
description: Cedar Breaks is a high-altitude amphitheater of Claron Formation pink cliffs near Brian Head. At over 10,000 feet, bristlecones cling to the rim above a badlands colosseum. It rivals Bryce's palette in a quieter setting.

title: Snow Canyon State Park
description: Snow Canyon mixes Navajo Sandstone cliffs with black basalt flows near St. George. Ancestral Puebloan and Paiute histories precede Mormon pioneer use of the canyon. Scenic drives and trails sample petrified dunes and lava tubes.

title: Dead Horse Point State Park
description: Dead Horse Point overlooks a dramatic Colorado River gooseneck near Canyonlands. Cowboy legend claims wild horses were once corralled on the narrow peninsula. Sunrise and sunset light the White Rim thousands of feet below.

title: Little Wild Horse Canyon Trailhead
description: Little Wild Horse is a classic San Rafael Swell slot canyon with narrows easily hiked by prepared visitors. The swell is a giant geologic uplift west of Green River. Nearby Goblin Valley makes this a popular weekend corridor.

title: Spiral Jetty Viewpoint
description: Robert Smithson's 1970 Spiral Jetty is a landmark of land art coiled into Great Salt Lake's north shore. Water levels alternately drown and expose the black basalt spiral. The remote causeway drive is part of the pilgrimage.

title: Golden Spike National Historical Park
description: Here the Union Pacific and Central Pacific rails met on May 10, 1869, completing the first transcontinental railroad. Replicas of Jupiter and No. 119 recreate the champagne ceremony. The site sits on the desolate Promontory Summit.

title: Antelope Island — Bridger Bay Area
description: Antelope Island is the Great Salt Lake's largest island, home to bison and pronghorn on lacustrine benches. Causeway access reveals the lake's salinity and bird-rich shores. Fielding Garr Ranch interprets early settlement on the island.

title: Flaming Gorge Dam Overlook
description: Flaming Gorge Dam (1964) impounds the Green River in a canyon John Wesley Powell named for its blazing red cliffs. Overlooks frame reservoir recreation and Colorado River Storage Project history. Sheep Creek and Red Canyon add scenic loops.

title: Trail Ridge Road — Rock Cut Area
description: Trail Ridge Road is the highest continuous paved highway in the U.S., cresting above 12,000 feet in Rocky Mountain National Park. Rock Cut viewpoints open onto alpine tundra that feels Arctic. Ute and Arapaho peoples crossed these high routes long before auto tourism.

title: Garden of the Gods — North Gateway
description: Garden of the Gods' vertical Fountain Formation fins rise against Pikes Peak on ancestral Ute lands. Railroad magnate Charles Elliott Perkins's family gifted the park for free public access. Balanced rock and Kissing Camels are classic Front Range icons.

title: Mesa Verde — Chapin Mesa Museum Area
description: Mesa Verde preserves Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings including Cliff Palace, among the most significant archaeological sites in North America. Chapin Mesa interprets centuries of mesa-top farming before the move into alcoves. The park was instrumental in early U.S. archaeological preservation.

title: Great Sand Dunes — High Dune Viewpoint
description: North America's tallest dunes rise against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains where creeks and prevailing winds trap sand. Medano Creek's seasonal surgelets fascinate visitors each spring. The dunefield is a rare alpine–desert juxtaposition.

title: Black Canyon of the Gunnison — Gunnison Point
description: The Black Canyon drops sheer into Precambrian gneiss so narrow that sunlight barely reaches the Gunnison River. Gunnison Point is the classic South Rim introduction. Extreme cliffs and hard rock made it one of the last Western canyons fully explored.

title: Maroon Bells Overlook
description: The Maroon Bells are twin fourteeners reflecting in Maroon Lake — among Colorado's most photographed peaks. Fragile alpine soils and heavy visitation led to bus-only seasons. Maroon Valley is iconic Elk Mountains scenery west of Aspen.

title: Independence Pass Summit
description: Independence Pass tops 12,095 feet on Highway 82 between Aspen and Twin Lakes, following old toll-road alignments. Summit tundra views stretch across the Continental Divide. The pass closes in winter under deep snow.

title: Royal Gorge Bridge Park
description: The Royal Gorge Bridge (1929) spans the Arkansas River more than 950 feet above the water. Once the world's highest suspension bridge, it remains a Front Range–Arkansas River tourism landmark. Steep gondolas and Via Ferrata routes add modern adventure layers.

title: Florissant Fossil Beds Visitor Center
description: Florissant preserves Eocene lakebed fossils — enormous petrified stumps and delicate insects — in volcanic ash shales. 19th-century collectors and later conservation battles shaped the monument. Quiet meadows sit beneath Pikes Peak country.

title: Colorado National Monument — Grand View
description: John Otto's trailbuilding zeal helped create Colorado National Monument's red-rock canyons above Grand Junction. Rim Rock Drive delivers sheer drops into Wingate Sandstone corridors. Independence Monument is the park's iconic freestanding tower.

title: Great Basin edge — Dinosaur NM Gates of Lodore
description: Gates of Lodore is where the Green River plunges into a dark canyon named by John Wesley Powell's 1869 expedition. Remote roads reach the put-in in Dinosaur National Monument's Colorado unit. It is holy ground for Western river-running history.

title: Dinosaur National Monument — Quarry Exhibit
description: The Carnegie Quarry wall displays hundreds of dinosaur bones left in place in Morrison Formation sandstone. Earl Douglass's 1909 discovery launched one of America's great fossil sites. The glass-enclosed wall is paleontology as architecture.

title: Devils Tower National Monument
description: Devils Tower is a sacred volcanic butte of columnar phonolite rising above the Belle Fourche River. It was America's first national monument (1906) and remains central to many Plains tribes' traditions. Climbers and cultural-respect closures share the tower.

title: Grand Teton — Mormon Row Barns
description: Mormon Row's weathered barns sit on an open sagebrush flat with the Teton Range as backdrop. Homesteaders from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints settled here in the 1890s. It is one of the most photographed vernacular landscapes in the Rockies.

title: Oxbow Bend — Grand Teton
description: Oxbow Bend is a slow curve of the Snake River reflecting Mount Moran at sunrise. Moose, otter, and waterfowl frequent the willows. It is a premier wildlife and landscape viewpoint on the park's north road.

title: Old Faithful Visitor Education Center
description: Old Faithful's predictable eruptions helped convince Congress to create Yellowstone — the world's first national park — in 1872. The geyser basin sits atop a volcanic caldera still restless today. Boardwalks protect fragile sinter while framing the iconic spout.

title: Grand Prismatic Spring Overlook
description: Grand Prismatic is the largest hot spring in the U.S., ringed by microbial mats that paint rainbow bands. The hill overlook reveals the full spectrum often missed from boardwalk level. It is Midway Geyser Basin's masterpiece of heat and color.

title: Artist Point — Yellowstone Canyon
description: Artist Point frames the Lower Falls of the Yellowstone River within the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. Hot hydrothermal alteration paints the canyon walls yellow and pink. Thomas Moran's paintings of this scene helped sell Yellowstone to the nation.

title: Lamar Valley Pullout — Yellowstone
description: Lamar Valley is often called America's Serengeti for bison herds and wolf-watching after reintroduction in the 1990s. Open glacial bottoms along the Lamar River define Yellowstone's northern range. Dawn and dusk are prime for wildlife.

title: Beartooth Pass Summit Area
description: Beartooth Highway climbs above 10,900 feet across alpine plateaus Charles Kuralt called one of America's most beautiful drives. Glacial tarns and tundra line the Wyoming–Montana crest. Snowfields often linger beside July pavement.

title: Bighorn Canyon — Devil Canyon Overlook
description: Devil Canyon Overlook peers into Bighorn Canyon's sheer walls above the Bighorn River reservoir. Crow Tribe homeland surrounds the recreation area. The viewpoint is among the most dramatic canyon rims in the northern Rockies.

title: Going-to-the-Sun Road — Logan Pass
description: Logan Pass sits on the Continental Divide at the apex of Going-to-the-Sun Road, an engineering marvel completed in 1932. Hidden Lake overlook and mountain goat habitat define Glacier National Park's alpine heart. Climate-driven glacier retreat is visible nearby.

title: Many Glacier Hotel Area
description: Many Glacier Hotel (1915) is a Swiss-chalet style lodge built by the Great Northern Railway to sell Glacier as America's Alps. Swiftcurrent Lake mirrors surrounding peaks and remaining glaciers. It remains a hub for boat tours and valley hikes.

title: Pompeys Pillar National Monument
description: Pompeys Pillar bears William Clark's 1806 signature — the only remaining physical evidence of Lewis and Clark along their route. The sandstone bluff overlooks the Yellowstone River. Crow and earlier peoples left older petroglyphs on the rock.

title: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
description: Little Bighorn marks the 1876 battle where Lakota, Northern Cheyenne, and Arapaho warriors defeated Lt. Col. Custer's battalion. Markers across the ridges interpret both U.S. Army and Indigenous perspectives. It remains one of the most consequential sites of the Plains wars.

title: Makoshika State Park — Cap Rock Area
description: Makoshika — 'bad earth' or 'badlands' in Lakota — is Montana's largest state park, with dinosaur fossils in Hell Creek Formation exposures. Cap rocks protect softer sediments into hoodoos near Glendive. Sunrise paints the badlands orange and lavender.

title: Glacier NP — Wild Goose Island Overlook
description: Wild Goose Island is a tiny islet in Saint Mary Lake framed by Glacier's eastern peaks. The roadside pullout is one of the park's most reproduced compositions. Morning calm often mirrors the whole scene.

title: Chaco Culture — Pueblo Bonito Overlook
description: Pueblo Bonito is the largest great house in Chaco Canyon, a ceremonial and economic hub of the Ancestral Puebloan world (850–1250 CE). Carefully aligned walls hint at astronomical knowledge. Washboard roads into the park preserve a sense of remoteness.

title: Bandelier National Monument — Frijoles Canyon
description: Bandelier protects cavates and masonry dwellings carved and built into volcanic tuff of the Pajarito Plateau. Ancestral Puebloan communities thrived along Frijoles Creek. Trails pass reconstructed talus pueblos and cliff rooms.

title: White Sands National Park Dunes Drive
description: White Sands holds the world's largest gypsum dunefield, blindingly white under desert sun. Dunes Drive loops into wave-like hills that migrate with wind. Missiles from White Sands Missile Range occasionally close the park — a Cold War neighbor.

title: Carlsbad Caverns — Natural Entrance Area
description: Carlsbad's Natural Entrance drops into a vast limestone cave system famed for the Big Room. Evening bat flights from the entrance amphitheater are a summer spectacle. Jim White's early explorations brought the caverns to national attention.

title: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument
description: Gila Cliff Dwellings occupy caves above the Gila River in the heart of America's first designated wilderness. Mogollon people built the rooms in the late 1200s. The remote mountain drive is part of the pilgrimage.

title: High Road to Taos — Santuario de Chimayó
description: El Santuario de Chimayó is a pilgrimage church famed for sacred earth and healing traditions. Built around 1816, it remains one of the most important Catholic pilgrimage sites in the U.S. The High Road weaves Hispanic village landscapes toward Taos.

title: Taos Pueblo Exterior Viewpoint Area
description: Taos Pueblo is a continuously inhabited multi-story adobe community and UNESCO World Heritage site. Red Willow Creek divides the north and south houses beneath Taos Mountain. Respect tribal rules — this is a living community, not a museum set.

title: Valles Caldera — Valle Grande Overlook
description: Valles Caldera is a 13-mile-wide volcanic caldera in the Jemez Mountains with vast grassy valle floors. Elk herds and historic ranching share the collapsed magma chamber. Overlooks reveal one of North America's clearest caldera landscapes.

title: Petroglyph National Monument — Rinconada Canyon
description: Tens of thousands of petroglyphs were pecked into Albuquerque's West Mesa basalt by Ancestral Puebloans and later Spanish settlers. Rinconada Canyon trails pass dense panels with volcanic vistas. Urban trails meet deep time on the city's edge.

title: Big Bend — Santa Elena Canyon Mouth
description: Santa Elena Canyon cuts a 1,500-foot limestone slot where the Rio Grande forms the U.S.–Mexico border. Canoes and hikers share the cool river corridor in desert heat. It is Big Bend's signature canyon mouth.

title: Big Bend — Balanced Rock Trailhead Area
description: Grapevine Hills' Balanced Rock is a granite tor puzzle in Big Bend's laccolith country. Short desert trails reach the window framing desert mountains. The Chisos and surrounding desert show Basin and Range tectonics in West Texas.

title: Guadalupe Peak Trailhead Area
description: Guadalupe Peak is Texas's highest point at 8,751 feet, rising from Capitan reef limestone of an ancient Permian sea. El Capitan's sheer face is the skyline landmark from U.S. 62/180. Trails climb through Chihuahuan Desert into high pines.

title: Palo Duro Canyon State Park Visitor Area
description: Palo Duro is the second-largest canyon in the U.S., carved by the Prairie Dog Town Fork of the Red River into Caprock Escarpment. Comanche and earlier peoples used the canyon; Charles Goodnight later ranched here. Spanish Skirts colorful layers define the Panhandle's Grand Canyon.

title: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
description: Enchanted Rock is a pink granite batholith dome sacred to Tonkawa and other peoples and a landmark for Spanish and Anglo travelers. Exfoliation slabs and vernal pools crown the summit. It is Central Texas's classic pluton hike.

title: San Antonio Missions — Mission San José
description: Mission San José y San Miguel de Aguayo — Queen of the Missions — anchored Spain's frontier evangelical and farming complex along the San Antonio River. UNESCO-listed missions tell Indigenous and colonial stories together. The rose window is an architectural icon.

title: Cape Blanco / Texas Coast — Mustang Island SP
description: Mustang Island State Park protects Gulf barrier-island dunes and beach south of Port Aransas. Whooping cranes winter nearby in Aransas NWR across the bay. Wind, surf, and coastal prairie define South Texas overlanding near the water.

title: Mount Rushmore National Memorial
description: Mount Rushmore's carved presidents were sculpted by Gutzon Borglum into the Black Hills' Harney Peak granite between 1927 and 1941. The site is contested sacred ground for the Lakota. It remains one of America's most visited monumental landscapes.

title: Badlands National Park — Pinnacles Overlook
description: Pinnacles Overlook surveys sharply eroded White River Badlands where fossil mammals record post-dinosaur evolution. Bison and bighorn reclaim mixed-grass prairie. Sunrise and sunset ignite the layered soft rock.

title: Jewel Cave National Monument
description: Jewel Cave is one of the world's longest caves, lined with calcite crystals that inspired its name. Discovery and exploration stories stretch from 1900 into modern survey pushes. It sits in ponderosa forest of the Black Hills.

title: Wind Cave National Park Visitor Area
description: Wind Cave features rare boxwork calcite formations and is sacred in Lakota emergence tradition. Above ground, one of the country's largest remaining mixed-grass prairies supports bison. Barometric 'breathing' at the entrance gave the cave its name.

title: Theodore Roosevelt NP — North Unit Overlook
description: The North Unit's River Bend overlooks frame Little Missouri badlands that shaped Theodore Roosevelt's conservation ethic after hunting and ranching here. Painted Canyon hues and cottonwood bottoms define western North Dakota. Elk and longhorn are often visible.

title: Knife River Indian Villages NHS
description: Knife River preserves Hidatsa and Mandan earthlodge village sites where Sakakawea lived before joining Lewis and Clark. Trade networks linked the Missouri River villages across the continent. Reconstructed lodges interpret Plains agricultural life.

title: Sleeping Bear Dunes — Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
description: Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore towers above Lake Michigan with perched dunes and an Anishinaabe origin legend of a mother bear and cubs. Pierce Stocking Drive delivers overlooks from forest to inland lakes. Bluff edges show how wind and ice sheets remade the coast.

title: Pictured Rocks — Miners Castle Overlook
description: Miners Castle is a colorful Cambrian sandstone turret on Lake Superior's Pictured Rocks shore. Mineral stains paint cliffs that became America's first national lakeshore. Kayaks and tour boats explore arches and sea caves along the same coast.

title: Tahquamenon Falls State Park
description: Upper Tahquamenon Falls drops about 50 feet across a 200-foot amber-colored curtain tinted by tannins. The falls sit in vast Upper Peninsula forest near Whitefish Point shipping lanes. It is Michigan's signature waterfall.

title: Isle Royale — Rock Harbor Visitor Area
description: Isle Royale is a roadless Lake Superior wilderness island famous for wolf–moose dynamics and ancient copper mining. Rock Harbor is the primary ferry and lodge gateway. Getting here is an expedition by boat or seaplane.

title: Apostle Islands — Little Sand Bay
description: Little Sand Bay is a mainland gateway to the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore's sea caves and lighthouses. Ojibwe homeland and brownstone quarrying history share the archipelago. Ice caves in winter draw rare cold-season pilgrimages.

title: Effigy Mounds National Monument
description: Effigy Mounds protects American Indian burial and ceremonial mounds shaped like animals along the Mississippi River bluffs. Woodland cultures built them over a thousand years ago. Trails interpret sacred landscapes still meaningful to descendant nations.

title: Gateway Arch National Park
description: Eero Saarinen's Gateway Arch (1965) commemorates St. Louis as the gateway to westward expansion. The underground museum revisits Lewis and Clark, Dred Scott, and river-city history. The 630-foot stainless span defines the Mississippi skyline.

title: Ozark National Scenic Riverways — Alley Spring
description: Alley Spring's turquoise pool and historic red mill sit on the Jacks Fork in the first national park area to protect a wild river system. Millions of gallons a day pour from dolomite springs. Ozark culture and canoe heritage define the region.

title: Hot Springs National Park Bathhouse Row
description: Bathhouse Row preserves Gilded Age spas built on protected thermal springs claimed as America's first federal reserve (1832). The park sits inside a working city. Quapaw and later spa culture made the valley a healing destination.

title: Buffalo National River — Tyler Bend
description: The Buffalo was America's first national river, protected in 1972 for free-flowing Ozark water. Tyler Bend offers gravel bars, bluffs, and access without a dam's interruption. Elk reintroduction added to the valley's wild character.

title: Mammoth Cave Historic Entrance Area
description: Mammoth Cave is the world's longest known cave system, with exploration still extending maps through limestone labyrinths. Enslaved guides were central to 19th-century tourism stories. The historic entrance area anchors a UNESCO World Heritage park.

title: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
description: Cumberland Gap was the natural notch through the Appalachians used by Indigenous peoples and later Daniel Boone's Wilderness Road. Thousands of settlers poured west through this pass. Pinnacle Overlook surveys three states.

title: Great Smoky Mountains — Newfound Gap
description: Newfound Gap sits on the Tennessee–North Carolina line at the crest of the most visited U.S. national park. FDR dedicated the park here in 1940. Spruce-fir forest and Appalachian Trail crossings define the gap.

title: Clingmans Dome Observation Tower
description: Clingmans Dome is the highest point in the Great Smokies and along the Appalachian Trail in the park. The spiral tower rises above Southern Appalachian spruce-fir. On clear days views stretch across multiple states.

title: Chickamauga & Chattanooga — Point Park
description: Point Park on Lookout Mountain commemorates the Civil War Battles for Chattanooga above the Tennessee River bend. Ochs Museum and batteries overlook the Moccasin Bend. It is among the earliest U.S. military parks.

title: Natchez Trace Parkway — Double Arch Bridge Area
description: The Natchez Trace follows a historic Indigenous and frontier route from Nashville toward Natchez. Near Birdsong Hollow, a modern double-arch bridge frames the parkway aesthetic. Mileposts interpret stands, inns, and boatmen's walks.

title: New Orleans — Jackson Square & St. Louis Cathedral
description: Jackson Square was the Plaza de Armas of French and Spanish colonial New Orleans, facing St. Louis Cathedral. The Cabildo and Presbytère frame Louisiana Purchase history. Street musicians keep the square a living Creole stage.

title: Everglades — Anhinga Trail Boardwalk
description: The Anhinga Trail offers close views of alligators, anhingas, and sawgrass marsh at the Everglades' edge. It interprets a wetland ecosystem unique in North America. Water management and restoration debates define the park's modern mission.

title: Dry Tortugas — Fort Jefferson Ferry Landing Area
description: Fort Jefferson is a massive Third System brick fort on Garden Key, 70 miles west of Key West. It held Civil War prisoners and later became a national park with living coral. Reaching it by ferry or seaplane is part of the quest.

title: Castillo de San Marcos National Monument
description: Castillo de San Marcos is the oldest masonry fort in the continental U.S., built by Spain beginning in 1672 to defend St. Augustine. Coquina walls absorbed British cannon fire. It anchors continuous European settlement history in Florida.

title: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex Area
description: The visitor complex interprets Cape Canaveral and Kennedy Space Center launches that sent Americans to orbit and the Moon. Saturn V exhibits and pads across the Banana River tell Cold War and STEM stories. Coastal wildlife refuges surround the spaceport.

title: Shenandoah — Big Meadows / Byrd VC Area
description: Big Meadows sits along Skyline Drive in Shenandoah National Park, created in the 1930s amid Appalachian resettlement controversies. Open meadows attract deer and stargazers. It is a classic Blue Ridge high-country stop.

title: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
description: Harpers Ferry sits at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah where John Brown's 1859 raid accelerated the path to Civil War. Armory ruins and steep streets pack layers of American conflict and industry. Appalachian Trail hikers pass through town.

title: New River Gorge — Canyon Rim Visitor Center
description: Canyon Rim overlooks the New River Gorge Bridge, once the world's longest single-span steel arch. The New River is among the continent's oldest rivers, cutting north through the Appalachians. Climbing, whitewater, and coal history share the gorge.

title: Assateague Island — Verrazzano Bridge Approach Area
description: Assateague is famous for wild horses descended from domestic stock on a barrier island shared by Maryland and Virginia. Dunes, marshes, and ocean beach shift constantly. Storm overwash continually rewrites the map.

title: Gettysburg National Military Park — Visitor Center Area
description: Gettysburg was the Civil War's pivotal July 1863 battle and the site of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address. Ridge lines and farm lanes remain readable landscapes of the three-day fight. It is among the most studied battlefields on Earth.

title: Independence National Historical Park — Liberty Bell Center
description: The Liberty Bell and Independence Hall anchor the founding documents of the United States in Philadelphia. UNESCO-listed buildings interpret revolution, slavery's contradictions, and constitutional debate. Old City streets retain 18th-century fabric.

title: Cape May Lighthouse
description: Cape May Light (1859) guides ships past the cape at Delaware Bay's mouth, tip of a Victorian seaside city. Migratory birds pour through in spectacular seasons. The lighthouse sits in a state park amid dunes and gun batteries.

title: Statue of Liberty / Liberty Island Ferry Approach Views
description: Liberty Enlightening the World (1886) became the defining immigrant welcome in New York Harbor. Bartholdi's statue and Bartholdi–Eiffel engineering sit on Fort Wood's star base. Ellis Island nearby completes the immigration story.

title: Niagara Falls — Prospect Point
description: Prospect Point overlooks the American Falls and Bridal Veil where the Niagara River plunges into a gorge toward Ontario. Hydroelectric history and honeymoon tourism shaped the border cities. Mist and thunder define one of North America's great waterfalls.

title: Acadia — Cadillac Mountain Summit
description: Cadillac Mountain is the highest point on the U.S. Atlantic coast and among the first sites of sunrise in winter. Carriage roads and granite summits define Acadia National Park on Mount Desert Island. Glacial polish and pink granite are classic Acadia.

title: Acadia — Jordan Pond House Area
description: Jordan Pond's clear water sits between the Bubbles with a historic tea-house tradition tied to early park tourism. Carriage roads by John D. Rockefeller Jr. circle the pond. It is Acadia's social and scenic heart.

title: Cape Cod National Seashore — Marconi Beach Area
description: Marconi Beach honors Guglielmo Marconi's 1903 transatlantic wireless station on Outer Cape Cod. National Seashore dunes and wave-cut cliffs show relentless Atlantic erosion. The Outer Cape remains a literary and ecological icon.

title: Minute Man National Historical Park — North Bridge
description: The North Bridge in Concord is where colonial militia engaged British regulars on April 19, 1775 — Emerson's 'shot heard round the world.' Battle Road traces the fighting toward Boston. Stone walls and farms preserve a revolutionary landscape.

title: Newport Cliff Walk — The Breakers Access Area
description: Newport's Cliff Walk threads between Gilded Age mansions and rocky Atlantic shore. The Breakers and neighbors display Vanderbilt-era wealth. Public right-of-way along the cliffs is a hard-won Rhode Island tradition.

title: Mystic Seaport Museum Waterfront
description: Mystic Seaport preserves a working 19th-century maritime village with the Charles W. Morgan whaleship. Connecticut's seafaring economy built ports that traded globally. Demonstrations keep wooden-boat skills alive.

title: Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park
description: This Woodstock estate interprets conservation history from George Perkins Marsh through Billings and Rockefeller stewardship. Carriage roads climb Mount Tom above the Ottauquechee Valley. It is a cradle narrative of American environmental thought.

title: Franconia Notch — Artist's Bluff / Echo Lake Area
description: Franconia Notch is a classic White Mountains pass with Echo Lake, cannon cliffs, and the former Old Man of the Mountain profile. I-93 threads a narrow state park corridor. Hikers and leaf-peepers share Appalachian granite country.

title: Saint-Gaudens National Historical Park
description: Augustus Saint-Gaudens's Cornish studio preserves the workplace of America's premier Beaux-Arts sculptor. Gardens and galleries sit above the Connecticut River. The site interprets how art colonies shaped New England culture.

title: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse Area
description: Cape Hatteras Light is the tallest brick lighthouse in the U.S., guarding Diamond Shoals — the Graveyard of the Atlantic. It was moved inland in 1999 to escape erosion. Barrier-island dynamics constantly threaten and remake the Outer Banks.

title: Wright Brothers National Memorial
description: Here Wilbur and Orville Wright achieved controlled powered flight on December 17, 1903, over Kill Devil Hills dunes. Monuments mark flight paths on the Outer Banks. Steady winds and soft sand made the site ideal for experiments.

title: Great Smoky — Cades Cove Loop Orientation
description: Cades Cove preserves an open valley of 19th-century farms, churches, and mills inside the Smokies. Deer, bears, and misty ridges draw heavy visitation. The loop road is a living museum of Appalachian settlement.

title: Congaree National Park — Boardwalk Loop
description: Congaree protects old-growth bottomland hardwood forest with some of the tallest trees in the eastern U.S. Elevated boardwalks cross floodplain that feels primeval. It is a rare remnant of a once-vast southeastern ecosystem.

title: Fort Sumter National Monument Ferry Landing
description: Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor is where the Civil War's first shots were fired in April 1861. The island fort's brick ruins interpret the siege that opened four years of conflict. Ferries leave from Liberty Square and Patriots Point.

title: Okefenokee — Suwannee Canal Recreation Area
description: Okefenokee is one of North America's largest blackwater swamp wildernesses, headwaters of the Suwannee River. Boardwalks and boats explore peat prairies and cypress. Seminole and earlier peoples knew its labyrinth long before park status.

title: Cumberland Island National Seashore Dock Area
description: Cumberland Island mixes wild beaches, feral horses, and Carnegie-era ruins reachable mainly by ferry. Dungeness mansion remnants speak to Gilded Age retreats. It is Georgia's largest barrier island preserve.

title: Little River Canyon National Preserve
description: Little River flows for most of its length atop Lookout Mountain before plunging into one of the deepest canyon systems in the East. Rim drives and falls overlooks feel unexpectedly western. Sandstone cliffs shelter rare plants.

title: Vicksburg National Military Park
description: Vicksburg's 1863 siege gave the Union control of the Mississippi River — a turning point of the Civil War. Monuments crown ridges above the river bends. USS Cairo's recovered ironclad is a rare surviving gunboat.

title: Hot Springs — Garvan Woodland Gardens Approach
description: Garvan Gardens occupy a Ouachita Mountains peninsula on Lake Hamilton with botanical collections and contemporary architecture. The Ouachitas are unusual east–west ridges in North America. Nearby thermal springs made Hot Springs famous.

title: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
description: Tallgrass Prairie preserves a remnant of the ecosystem that once covered much of the Great Plains. Flint Hills ranching continues beside restored prairie and a historic ranch headquarters. Bison graze where homesteaders met endless grass.

title: Scotts Bluff National Monument
description: Scotts Bluff was a landmark on the Oregon, California, and Mormon Pioneer trails rising above the North Platte Valley. Wagon ruts and summit views interpret the great overland migration. Mitchell Pass funneled emigrants west.

title: Chimney Rock National Historic Site
description: Chimney Rock's spire was the most noted landmark of the Oregon Trail, recorded in countless emigrant diaries. Soft Brule clay continues to erode the spire's height. It signaled the approach to the Rockies for wagon companies.

title: Homestead National Historical Park
description: Homestead interprets the 1862 Homestead Act that transferred vast public lands to private farms — reshaping Indigenous homelands and the Plains. Tallgrass restoration surrounds the heritage center. It is the flagship site for that land-policy story.

title: Fort Laramie National Historic Site
description: Fort Laramie was the pivotal trading post and military fort of the Northern Plains overland trails. Treaties signed here attempted — and often failed — to manage conflict on Indigenous lands. Restored buildings sit at the Laramie and North Platte confluence.

title: Register Cliff State Historic Site
description: Emigrants carved names into Register Cliff soft sandstone along the Oregon Trail near Guernsey. Nearby deep wagon ruts cut into stone. It is personal graffiti as primary source for westward migration.

title: Legend Rock Petroglyph Site
description: Legend Rock hosts hundreds of Indigenous petroglyphs on sandstone cliffs in the Bighorn Basin. Panels span millennia of Plains visual culture. Remote BLM/state management aims to protect fragile rock art.

title: Bighorn Medicine Wheel
description: The Medicine Wheel on Medicine Mountain is a sacred stone circle at nearly 10,000 feet with cairns and spokes. Many tribes continue ceremonial use; visitors should stay on paths and show respect. Alpine tundra surrounds the National Historic Landmark.

title: Fossil Butte National Monument
description: Fossil Butte preserves Eocene Fossil Lake fishes and plants in paper-thin limestone — some of the world's finest fossils. The visitor center displays extraordinary complete specimens. Quiet high desert surrounds Kemmerer country.

title: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone — Lookout Point
description: Lookout Point peers toward Lower Falls within Yellowstone's vividly colored canyon. Hydrothermal alteration paints rhyolite walls. Early park artists and photographers made this gorge a national symbol.

title: Signal Mountain Summit Road
description: Signal Mountain's summit road offers 360° views over Jackson Lake, the Tetons, and the valley floor. Wildfire lookouts once used the peak. It is a short drive to a grand Teton panorama.

title: Craig Thomas Discovery Center Area — Moose
description: The Craig Thomas Discovery and Visitor Center orients travelers to Grand Teton ecology and human history at Moose. The Snake River and Teton fault scarps are visible nearby. It is the park's modern interpretive gateway.

title: Lake Louise Lakeshore Trailhead
description: Lake Louise is a glacial lake at the foot of the Victoria Glacier, made famous by the Chateau Lake Louise railway hotel era. Stoney Nakoda and other nations know these valleys intimately. Turquoise water comes from fine rock flour suspended in meltwater.

title: Moraine Lake Rockpile Viewpoint
description: Moraine Lake sits in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, once featured on Canadian currency. The rockpile viewpoint frames Wenkchemna Peaks above impossibly blue water. Access is timed in peak season to protect the fragile corridor.

title: Banff — Surprise Corner Viewpoint
description: Surprise Corner overlooks the Banff Springs Hotel and Bow River falls area — a classic Canadian Pacific Railway tourism tableau. Hot springs discovery in the 1880s led to Banff becoming Canada's first national park. Cascade Mountain anchors the skyline.

title: Banff — Sulphur Mountain Gondola Base
description: Sulphur Mountain rises above Banff townsite with a boardwalk to a cosmic-ray station historic site. Hot springs on the mountain's flank sparked park creation. Panoramas take in the Bow Valley's classic U-shape.

title: Icefields Parkway — Bow Lake Num-Ti-Jah Area
description: Bow Lake mirrors Crowfoot Glacier along the Icefields Parkway, one of the world's great mountain drives. Num-Ti-Jah Lodge recalls early guide Jimmy Simpson's era. The parkway links Banff and Jasper through continuous rock and ice.

title: Peyto Lake Overlook
description: Peyto Lake's wolf-head outline and vivid turquoise make it an Icefields Parkway icon. A short walk from Bow Summit reaches the classic viewpoint. Glacial silt refracts light into striking blues and greens.

title: Columbia Icefield — Athabasca Glacier Viewpoint
description: Athabasca Glacier spills from the Columbia Icefield — a hydrological apex feeding oceans via different rivers. Roadside markers show dramatic 20th-century retreat. It is the most visited glacier in North America.

title: Parker Ridge Trailhead — Icefields Parkway
description: Parker Ridge climbs quickly to views of the Saskatchewan Glacier arm of the Columbia Icefield. Hike traffic is heavy because the reward-to-effort ratio is exceptional. Alpine meadows sit above the parkway's northern stretch.

title: Jasper — Medicine Lake Viewpoint
description: Medicine Lake is a disappearing lake that drains through sinkholes into a vast karst system toward Maligne Canyon. In late summer the 'lake' can shrink to a braided river. Indigenous knowledge long noted its mysterious vanishing.

title: Maligne Canyon Upper Bridges
description: Maligne Canyon is a deep limestone slot carved by the Maligne River just below Jasper townsite. Bridges cross slots where the river disappears into caves. Winter ice walks reveal a different character.

title: Maligne Lake — Spirit Island Boat Dock Area
description: Spirit Island is a tiny islet in Maligne Lake framed by the Bald Hills — one of the most reproduced images in the Canadian Rockies. Stoney Nakoda cultural significance attaches to the site. Boat tours make the classic vantage reachable.

title: Mount Edith Cavell Meadows Trailhead
description: Mount Edith Cavell rises above Angel Glacier and Cavell Pond with icebergs calving into milky water. Named for a World War I nurse, the peak is a Jasper icon. Recent glacier retreat has reshaped the forefield rapidly.

title: Miette Hot Springs Area
description: Miette Hot Springs are the hottest in the Canadian Rockies, flowing from limestone on Jasper's east side. A historic aquacourt tradition continues with mountain views. Elk often graze the approach road meadows.

title: Yoho — Emerald Lake Lodge Area
description: Emerald Lake's vivid color sits beneath the President Range in Yoho National Park. A circuit trail and historic lodge recall early CPR tourism. The Burgess Shale quarries nearby revolutionized understanding of Cambrian life.

title: Yoho — Takakkaw Falls Viewpoint
description: Takakkaw Falls plunges from the Daly Glacier in one of Canada's highest waterfalls. The Cree-derived name means 'it is magnificent.' Yoho Valley Road access is seasonal and steep.

title: Kicking Horse Pass — Spiral Tunnels Viewpoint
description: The Spiral Tunnels solved the CPR's dangerous grade down from Kicking Horse Pass after the original Big Hill proved deadly. Viewing areas interpret trains looping inside the mountains. The pass is a Continental Divide landmark.

title: Glacier NP Canada — Rogers Pass Discovery Centre
description: Rogers Pass was the CPR's snowbound ordeal through the Selkirks, later tamed by the Connaught and Mount Macdonald tunnels and avalanche defenses. The discovery centre interprets railway sacrifice and mountain weather. Today's Highway 1 still closes for controlled slides.

title: Mount Revelstoke — Meadows in the Sky Parkway
description: Meadows in the Sky Parkway climbs Mount Revelstoke through interior rainforest into subalpine flower meadows. Summit boardwalks offer Selkirk panoramas. It is a rare drive-to-alpine experience in a Canadian national park.

title: Waterton Lakes — Prince of Wales Hotel Viewpoint
description: The Prince of Wales Hotel (1927) perches above Upper Waterton Lake where the Rockies meet the prairie. Waterton–Glacier is an International Peace Park. Wind here is famously relentless.

title: Waterton — Red Rock Canyon Parking
description: Red Rock Canyon cuts through bright argillite in Waterton's northwest corner. Shallow water over crimson beds makes a family-friendly geologic walk. The color comes from ancient iron-rich sediments.

title: Kootenay — Radium Hot Springs Pools Area
description: Radium Hot Springs sit at the southwestern gate of Kootenay National Park in a rocky canyon of the Kootenay River. Aquacourt tradition dates to early park tourism. Iron-rich water leaves a mineral tint.

title: Kootenay — Marble Canyon Bridge
description: Marble Canyon is a tight dolomite slot carved by Tokumm Creek near the Continental Divide. Bridges cross turquoise water in a narrow chasm. A 2003 fire reshaped surrounding forest views.

title: Pacific Rim — Long Beach Breaker Area
description: Long Beach in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve is a vast surf-pounded strand on Vancouver Island's west coast. Nuu-chah-nulth territories encompass these shores. Fog, cedars, and Pacific swell define the Rainforest Coast.

title: Tofino — Wickaninnish Beach Access
description: Wickaninnish Beach is a signature Pacific Rim strand named in association with Nuu-chah-nulth leadership history. Storm watching in winter draws visitors for big swell days. Dune grass and coastal forest back the sand.

title: Cathedral Grove — MacMillan Provincial Park
description: Cathedral Grove protects monumental Douglas-fir and cedar stands along Highway 4 to Port Alberni. Some trees are centuries old — a remnant of coastal old growth. Boardwalks try to balance access and root protection.

title: Whistler — Peak 2 Peak / Roundhouse Base Area
