description: Whistler Blackcomb grew from a 1960s ski ambition into an Olympic host mountain resort (2010). Alpine trails and glaciers sit above a purpose-built village. Coast Mountains scenery anchors year-round tourism.

title: Sea to Sky — Shannon Falls Provincial Park
description: Shannon Falls drops 335 metres near Squamish, one of British Columbia's highest waterfalls. It sits on the Sea to Sky Highway between Vancouver and Whistler. Granite walls nearby fuel a world-famous climbing scene.

title: Stawamus Chief Viewpoint Area
description: The Stawamus Chief is a massive granite face rising above Squamish — a Coast Belt climbing icon. Hikers use steep trails with chains to summit viewpoints. The Chief defines Squamish's skyline at Howe Sound.

title: Hope Slide Viewpoint
description: The 1965 Hope Slide buried Highway 3 under millions of tonnes of rock, killing four motorists. A viewpoint interprets the scar still visible on the mountainside. It is a sobering lesson in Fraser Valley geology.

title: Fort Langley National Historic Site
description: Fort Langley was a Hudson's Bay Company depot and the site where British Columbia was proclaimed a crown colony in 1858. Reconstructed palisades interpret fur-trade life on the Fraser. It anchors the Lower Mainland's colonial origin story.

title: Stanley Park — Prospect Point
description: Prospect Point overlooks Lions Gate Bridge and the First Narrows where Burrard Inlet meets open views toward the North Shore mountains. Stanley Park occupies ancient Coast Salish village sites. Totem poles and seawall paths layer histories.

title: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park Area
description: Capilano's suspension bridge has drawn visitors across a rainforest canyon since 1889. Modern park additions sit among Douglas-fir on Capilano River. It is early Vancouver tourism still going strong.

title: Harrison Hot Springs Waterfront
description: Harrison Hot Springs has been a mineral-soak destination since the 19th century at the south end of Harrison Lake. Mountains rise directly from the lake into the Coast Range. Sts'ailes and other nations' histories precede resort development.

title: Okanagan — Knox Mountain Park Lookout
description: Knox Mountain overlooks Kelowna and Okanagan Lake in British Columbia's dry interior fruit-and-wine country. Grassland and ponderosa slopes show the rainshadow climate. The lake is a summer recreation spine of the valley.

title: Myra Canyon Trestles — Kettle Valley Rail Trail
description: Myra Canyon's rebuilt trestles carry the Kettle Valley Rail Trail across dramatic side canyons above Kelowna. Original railway engineering opened the Okanagan to rail; fire later destroyed then restored trestles. Cycling the canyon is a prairie-to-peak contrast.

title: Muncho Lake Provincial Park — Strawberry Flats
description: Muncho Lake's jade waters sit along the Alaska Highway amid the northern Rockies. Folded mountains plunge toward one of BC's most beautiful roadside lakes. It is a landmark of the long drive toward Yukon.

title: Liard River Hot Springs Provincial Park
description: Liard Hot Springs are a lush warm oasis on the Alaska Highway where boreal forest meets tropical-feeling boards through warm swamps. Moose sometimes wade the warm outlets. It is the classic soak for northbound travelers.

title: Sign Post Forest — Watson Lake
description: Watson Lake's Sign Post Forest began in 1942 when a homesick GI put up a sign pointing toward his hometown during Alaska Highway construction. Tens of thousands of signs now cover the grove. It is roadside folk culture of the North.

title: Yukon — Emerald Lake Viewpoint
description: Emerald Lake south of Whitehorse glows from marl (calcium carbonate) reflecting in shallow water. It is a quick scenic stop on the South Klondike Highway toward Skagway. Mountains frame a color that seems unreal.

title: Carcross Desert Wayside
description: Carcross Desert is a small dune field of glacial lake sediments claimed as one of the world's smallest deserts. Tagish and Tlingit histories surround the crossroads community. The Klondike Gold Rush railway corridor passes nearby.

title: White Pass Summit — Klondike Highway
description: White Pass was a brutal gold-rush gateway from Skagway toward the Yukon interior, later crossed by the White Pass & Yukon Route railway. The highway summit still feels alpine and windswept. It commemorates stampeders of 1897–99.

title: Miles Canyon Bridge — Whitehorse
description: Miles Canyon's basalt cliffs once terrified Klondike stampeders on the Yukon River before a tramway bypassed the rapids. A suspension footbridge now spans quieter water above Schwatka Lake. It sits minutes from downtown Whitehorse.

title: SS Klondike National Historic Site
description: SS Klondike was a sternwheeler that hauled freight on the Yukon River in the sternwheeler era after the gold rush. Restored onshore in Whitehorse, it interprets river transport that built the territory. The Yukon's lifeline was once paddlewheels.

title: Dawson City — Palace Grand Theatre Area
description: Dawson City was the boomtown capital of the Klondike Gold Rush, with boardwalk streets and restored theatres. Permafrost and isolation shaped architecture and legend. It remains a living town at the Yukon and Klondike rivers' confluence.

title: Dempster Highway — Tombstone Territorial Park Interpretive
description: Tombstone's jagged peaks rise along the Dempster Highway — Canada's road to the Arctic Ocean via Inuvik. Interpretive centres explain subarctic ecology and Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in homeland. Fall colors here are legendary.

title: Dempster — Engineer Creek Campground Area
description: Engineer Creek is a classic Dempster Highway stop in continuous wilderness toward the Richardson Mountains. The gravel highway is a modern Indigenous and resource corridor into the Western Arctic. Services are scarce — preparation matters.

title: Inuvik — Our Lady of Victory Igloo Church
description: Inuvik's Igloo Church is a landmark of Canada's Arctic town built for the Mackenzie Delta. The Dempster Highway's end (before the Tuktoyaktuk all-season extension) made Inuvik a pilgrimage for overlanders. Midnight sun and permafrost define life here.

title: Tuktoyaktuk — Pingos and Arctic Ocean Shore
description: Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean became reachable by all-season road in 2017, transforming Inuvialuit community access. Pingos — ice-cored hills — are signature landforms. Dipping a toe in the Arctic Ocean is an overlanding rite.

title: Nahanni — Virginia Falls (from park context / Fort Simpson Gateway)
description: Fort Simpson is the primary gateway community for Nahanni National Park Reserve, where Virginia Falls dwarfs Niagara on the South Nahanni River. UNESCO-listed mountain wilderness draws paddlers by floatplane. The Dehcho region is Dene homeland.

title: Wood Buffalo — Pine Lake Area Access
description: Wood Buffalo National Park is North America's largest national park, protecting whooping crane nesting habitat and free-roaming wood bison. Karst sinkhole lakes like Pine Lake add geologic oddity. Access is long and logistical.

title: Elk Island National Park — Astotin Lake Area
description: Elk Island protects plains and wood bison herds in aspen parkland east of Edmonton — a key source for bison restoration projects. Astotin Lake trails offer easy wildlife viewing. It is a conservation success story in miniature.

title: Writing-on-Stone / Áísínai'pi — Visitor Centre Area
description: Áísínai'pi (Writing-on-Stone) holds one of the largest concentrations of Plains Indigenous rock art along the Milk River. Hoodoos and sandstone cliffs form a sacred landscape. UNESCO recognition underscores its cultural importance.

title: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Head-Smashed-In is a UNESCO buffalo jump used for nearly 6,000 years by Plains peoples to harvest bison. Cliffs and drive lanes remain readable on the land. The interpretive centre is among Canada's finest Indigenous history sites.

title: Dinosaurs Provincial Park Overlook
description: Dinosaur Provincial Park's badlands yield exceptional Cretaceous dinosaur fossils in the Judith River Group. UNESCO status reflects both paleontology and striking eroded terrain. Sunset light on hoodoos is unforgettable.

title: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park — Gap Road Area
description: Cypress Hills rise as a forested plateau above the prairie — an erosional remnant that escaped glaciation in places. Fort Walsh nearby interprets NWMP history. The hills are a sky island of lodgepole and aspen.

title: Prince Albert National Park — Waskesiu Lake
description: Waskesiu is the resort community inside Prince Albert National Park, where Grey Owl once lived and wrote. Boreal lakes and trails sit at the prairie–forest transition. It is central Saskatchewan's signature park gateway.

title: Batoche National Historic Site
description: Batoche was the seat of Louis Riel's Provisional Government and the site of the 1885 Battle of Batoche ending the North-West Resistance. Métis river-lot farms line the South Saskatchewan. It is foundational to Métis nation history.

title: Riding Mountain — Clear Lake Townsite Area
description: Riding Mountain is a forested highland island in a prairie sea, with bison enclosures and Clear Lake recreation. Indigenous and park-creation histories intertwine. Wildlife viewing is excellent along the escarpment.

title: The Forks National Historic Site — Winnipeg
description: The Forks at the Assiniboine and Red rivers has been a meeting place for 6,000 years — Indigenous trade, fur trade, and modern Winnipeg culture. Walkways and markets sit on layered archaeology. It remains the city's gathering heart.

title: Churchill — Cape Merry Battery Area
description: Cape Merry guards the mouth of the Churchill River near Hudson Bay, with forts tied to fur-trade wars. Polar bears stage here in fall waiting for ice. It is one of the most remote iconic wildlife destinations in Canada.

title: Sleeping Giant — Thunder Bay Lookout Area
description: The Sleeping Giant peninsula silhouette defines Thunder Bay's Lake Superior skyline and Anishinaabe legend. Overlooks and Sibley Peninsula trails interpret the formation. Superior's cold inland sea dominates the mood.

title: Pukaskwa — Hattie Cove Trailheads
description: Hattie Cove is the main access to Pukaskwa National Park on Lake Superior's wild northeast shore. Coastal trails follow headlands in Anishinaabe territory. It is Ontario's remote Superior wilderness park.

title: Lake Superior Provincial Park — Old Woman Bay
description: Old Woman Bay's pebble beach sits beneath cliffs said to resemble a face in the rock. The Trans-Canada hugs Superior through this provincial park. Agate hunting and cold swells define the shore.

title: Agawa Rock Pictographs — Lake Superior PP
description: Agawa Rock's cliffside pictographs are sacred Anishinaabe images reachable by a rugged shore scramble. Mishipeshu the water panther is among the figures. Superior's waves sometimes spray the gallery.

title: Bruce Peninsula — Grotto / Cyprus Lake Area
description: The Grotto is a wave-cut sea cave in dolostone cliffs of Bruce Peninsula National Park on Georgian Bay. Turquoise water and Niagara Escarpment geology draw heavy visitation. Flowerpot Island's stacks continue the theme offshore.

title: Fathom Five — Tobermory Harbour
description: Tobermory is the gateway to Fathom Five National Marine Park, Canada's first, protecting shipwrecks and clear Georgian Bay shallows. Chiichewing / Big Tub Lighthouse frames the harbor. Ferry links to Manitoulin begin here.

title: Manitoulin — Cup and Saucer Trailhead Area
description: Cup and Saucer offers Niagara Escarpment cliff views on Manitoulin, the world's largest freshwater island. Anishinaabe cultural presence is strong across the island. Overlooks take in farmland and forest mosaic.

title: Algonquin — Lake of Two Rivers Beach Area
description: Lake of Two Rivers sits on Highway 60 through Algonquin Provincial Park — Ontario's famous canoe-country park founded in 1893. Tom Thomson and the Group of Seven painted these woods. Moose and loons remain icons.

title: Algonquin — Lookout Trail / Cache Lake Area
description: Highway 60 lookouts survey Algonquin's hardwood hills famous for fall color. Cache Lake hosted early park administration and lodge culture. The corridor balances access with interior wilderness paddling routes.

title: Ottawa — Parliament Hill East Block Area
description: Parliament Hill's Gothic Revival buildings house Canada's federal legislature overlooking the Ottawa River. The site was chosen as Queen Victoria's capital for the young Dominion. Changing of the Guard and the Peace Tower define national ritual.

title: Thousand Islands — Rockport / Skydeck Area
description: The Thousand Islands stud the St. Lawrence where ice-sheet flooding drowned a granite landscape. Castles and shipping lanes share the international river. Skydeck views interpret Loyalist and Gilded Age cottage eras.

title: Niagara Falls ON — Table Rock Centre Area
description: Table Rock sits beside Horseshoe Falls, the largest of the Niagara complex by volume. Canadian side walkways deliver spray-in-the-face views. Hydroelectric tunnels and tourism have shaped the border for two centuries.

title: Point Pelee National Park Tip
description: Point Pelee is mainland Canada's southernmost tip and a world-class migratory bird funnel. Marsh boardwalks and a sand tip into Lake Erie define the park. Fall hawk and songbird migrations are legendary.

title: Québec City — Terrasse Dufferin & Château Frontenac
description: Terrasse Dufferin overlooks the St. Lawrence beneath the iconic Château Frontenac in UNESCO Old Québec. French colonial fortifications and Cap Diamant cliffs shape North America's most European cityscape. It is the heart of New France heritage.

title: Montmorency Falls Park
description: Montmorency Falls drops higher than Niagara just east of Québec City where the Montmorency meets the St. Lawrence. Suspension bridges and cable cars frame the curtain. Military history nearby includes the 1759 Cap Rouge campaigns.

title: Charlevoix — Cap-aux-Oies / River Viewpoint Area
description: Charlevoix's half-graben landscape — partly shaped by an ancient impact crater — rolls to the St. Lawrence estuary. Whale-watching waters begin as the river widens. UNESCO biosphere status recognizes the cultural landscape.

title: Saguenay Fjord — Parc national lookout (Baie-Éternité area)
description: The Saguenay Fjord cuts a deep glacial trough into the Canadian Shield with walls over 400 metres. Belugas frequent the St. Lawrence confluence. Baie-Éternité cliffs are among Eastern Canada's most dramatic.

title: Gaspésie — Percé Rock Viewpoint
description: Rocher Percé's pierced limestone stack is the Gaspé Peninsula's icon, changing with tides and rockfalls. Nearby Île Bonaventure hosts a huge gannet colony. It has drawn pilgrims and painters for centuries.

title: Forillon National Park — Cap-Bon-Ami
description: Cap-Bon-Ami's cliffs mark the Appalachians' eastern plunge into the Gulf of St. Lawrence at Forillon. Whale spouts and seabirds share the headland. Expropriation stories of park creation remain part of local memory.

title: Tadoussac — Pointe de l'Islet Whale Lookout
description: Tadoussac sits at the Saguenay–St. Lawrence confluence, a historic Basque whaling and First Nations trade site. Modern whale-watching capital energy fills the bay. Pointe de l'Islet is an easy shore-based lookout.

title: Mauricie — Saint-Maurice River Corridor Lookout
description: La Mauricie National Park protects Laurentian lakes and hills between Montréal and Québec. Former logging country now hosts canoe routes and wolves. Fall color over the Saint-Maurice hills is outstanding.

title: Kouchibouguac — Kellys Beach Boardwalk
description: Kellys Beach boardwalk crosses lagoons to a wide Gulf of St. Lawrence strand in Kouchibouguac National Park. Mi'kmaq homeland and Acadian coastal culture surround the park. Pipewort and shorebirds share the dunes.

title: Fundy National Park — Herring Cove Area
description: Fundy National Park fronts the Bay of Fundy, home to the world's highest tides. Herring Cove and nearby falls show the tidal range's power. Forests behind the shore hide a dense Acadian–Appalachian mosaic.

title: Hopewell Rocks Provincial Park
description: Hopewell Rocks are flowerpot sea stacks you can walk among at low tide and paddle past at high tide. Fundy's tidal range creates the daily transformation. Soft sandstone sculpture is ongoing.

title: Saint John — Reversing Falls Lookout
description: Reversing Falls rapids change direction as Fundy tides overpower the Saint John River outflow. Lookouts interpret one of the Atlantic coast's oddest hydrologic shows. The port city grew around this energy.

title: Confederation Bridge Viewpoint — Cape Jourimain
description: Cape Jourimain looks toward Confederation Bridge, the 13-km link opened in 1997 connecting PEI to the mainland. Marshes around the cape are a national wildlife area. The bridge transformed Island access.

title: Prince Edward Island NP — Green Gables Area
description: Green Gables farmhouse inspired Lucy Maud Montgomery's Anne of Green Gables, drawing literary pilgrims to Cavendish. Dunes and red sandstone cliffs of PEI National Park sit nearby. Potato fields and North Shore beaches define the Island.

title: PEI NP — Cavendish Beach Dunes
description: Cavendish Beach's dunes and red sand are Prince Edward Island National Park signatures on the Gulf Shore. Dynamic dune systems need boardwalk discipline. Anne tourism and beach days coexist here.

title: Cape Breton — Skyline Trailhead (Cabot Trail)
description: The Skyline Trail on the Cabot Trail offers boardwalk ridge views over the Gulf of St. Lawrence in Cape Breton Highlands National Park. Sunset silhouettes are famous. Moose and Acadian–Gaelic cultural layers share the highlands.

title: Cabot Trail — Cap Rouge Lookoff
description: Cap Rouge lookoffs survey French Mountain and coast along one of the world's great scenic drives. The Cabot Trail encircles highland plateaus plunging to the sea. Weather changes fast on exposed headlands.

title: Louisbourg — Fortress National Historic Site
description: The Fortress of Louisbourg is a reconstructed 18th-century French fortified town — once a key North Atlantic stronghold. Sieges of 1745 and 1758 shaped imperial fortunes. Fog and Atlantic swell set the mood.

title: Peggy's Cove Lighthouse
description: Peggy's Cove Light sits on wave-washed granite of St. Margarets Bay, among Canada's most photographed coastal scenes. Fishing village life continues amid tourism. The rocks are beautifully dangerous in swell.

title: Halifax — Citadel National Historic Site
description: Halifax Citadel's star fort has watched the harbor since the mid-1800s, continuing earlier British defenses. Noon gun tradition persists. The hill interprets Halifax's role as an imperial naval town.

title: Kejimkujik National Park Seaside — St. Catherine's River Beach
description: Kejimkujik Seaside protects remote beaches and bog on Nova Scotia's southwest shore, separate from the inland Mi'kmaq canoe park unit. Harbour seals haul out on rocks. It is a quiet Atlantic counterpoint to busier Cabot Trail scenes.

title: Gros Morne — Western Brook Pond Trailhead
description: Western Brook Pond is a landlocked glacial fjord with 600-metre cliffs inside Gros Morne National Park, a UNESCO site showcasing plate tectonics. Boat tours enter after a marsh boardwalk hike. It is Newfoundland's signature inland fjord.

title: Gros Morne — Tablelands Trailhead
description: The Tablelands expose orange peridotite mantle rock — normally deep underground — evidence of the ancient Iapetus Ocean's closure. The barren slopes look like another planet. Gros Morne's geology rewrote Appalachian science.

title: L'Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site
description: L'Anse aux Meadows is the only confirmed Norse site in North America, dating to ~1000 CE. Reconstructed sod buildings interpret Vinland sagas meeting archaeology. It sits at Newfoundland's northern tip on the Strait of Belle Isle.

title: Twillingate — Long Point Lighthouse
description: Long Point Light overlooks Iceberg Alley near Twillingate, where Greenland ice drifts south in spring. Fishing heritage and quiet lanes define Notre Dame Bay towns. Whale spouts often join the bergs.

title: Cape Spear Lighthouse National Historic Site
description: Cape Spear is the easternmost point in North America (excluding Greenland), with a historic light guarding approaches to St. John's. WWII gun batteries share the headland. Sunrise here is among the continent's first.

title: Signal Hill National Historic Site
description: Signal Hill rises above St. John's Narrows where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901. Cabot Tower and harbor defenses interpret centuries of North Atlantic strategy. The North Head Trail is spectacular.

title: Terra Nova National Park — Newman Sound Area
description: Terra Nova is Newfoundland's first national park, protecting boreal forest meeting sheltered Atlantic reaches. Newman Sound kayak routes explore quiet coves. It is a gentler counterpoint to Gros Morne's drama.

title: Fundy Trail Parkway — Flowerpot Rock Area
description: The Fundy Trail Parkway follows cliff tops above some of the bay's least-developed shoreline. Flowerpot formations and lookoffs interpret extreme tides. It is a purpose-built scenic drive for slow travel.

title: Kejimkujik Inland — Merrymakedge Beach Area
description: Inland Kejimkujik protects Mi'kmaq canoe routes, petroglyphs, and loon lakes of southwest Nova Scotia. Merrymakedge is a family beach on Kejimkujik Lake. Cultural interpretation with Mi'kmaq partners is central to the park.

title: Redwood — Lady Bird Johnson Grove Trailhead
description: Lady Bird Johnson Grove preserves towering coast redwoods in Redwood National and State Parks. Dedication in 1969 honored the First Lady's conservation advocacy. Fog drip and hush define the grove.

title: Jedediah Smith — Stout Grove Area
description: Stout Grove sits along the Smith River among some of the largest coast redwoods. Ferns and flat alluvial soil grow monumental trees. It is a cathedral of the northern parks complex.

title: Lassen — Bumpass Hell Boardwalk Area
description: Bumpass Hell is Lassen's largest hydrothermal area — boiling pools and mudpots named for a cowboy who scalded his leg. Boardwalks cross a living volcanic plumbing system. It shows Cascades heat without a major eruption.

title: Mount Rainier — Paradise Visitor Center Area
description: Paradise is Mount Rainier's most famous meadow belt, with wildflowers beneath the heavily glaciated stratovolcano. Historic lodges and guide culture date to early park tourism. Nisqually Glacier views explain the mountain's power.

title: Mount Rainier — Sunrise Visitor Area
description: Sunrise is the highest reach by paved road in the park, on Rainier's east side with Emmons Glacier views. Burroughs Mountain trails enter alpine tundra. Crowds chase alpenglow on clear evenings.

title: Olympic — Hurricane Ridge Wildlife Overlooks
description: Hurricane Ridge overlooks often deliver deer and distant glacier views across the Olympic interior. The rainshadow effect creates surprisingly dry subalpine meadows. Port Angeles lights glitter far below at night.

title: North Cascades — Washington Pass Overlook
description: Washington Pass Overlook surveys Liberty Bell Mountain and Early Winters Spires along the North Cascades Highway. Granite spires define a climber's skyline. The highway is typically seasonal through heavy snow country.

title: San Juan Island — American Camp Visitor Area
description: American Camp interprets the 1859 Pig War standoff that nearly sparked U.S.–British conflict over the San Juans. Prairies and Strait of Juan de Fuca views remain open. Killer whales sometimes pass offshore.

title: Columbia River Gorge — Crown Point Vista House
description: Vista House (1918) crowns Crown Point as an early Historic Columbia River Highway rest stop. The octagonal building overlooks a bend of the Gorge. It symbolizes the first scenic highway movement in the West.

title: Cannon Beach — Haystack Rock Tidepool Area
description: Haystack Rock is a 235-foot sea stack and seabird colony on Cannon Beach, among Oregon Coast icons. Tidepools at low water reveal starfish and anemones. The Needles stacks continue the skyline south.

title: Newberry National Volcanic Monument — Lava Lands
description: Lava Lands Visitor Center interprets Newberry Volcano's vast caldera, lava flows, and the Lava River Cave. Paulina and East Lakes sit inside the caldera. Obsidian flows draw rockhounds and geologists.

title: Three Capes — Cape Lookout Trailhead
description: Cape Lookout juts into the Pacific on the Three Capes Scenic Route with a trail to a whale-watching tip. Sitka spruce and cliffs define the headland. It is a classic Tillamook Coast hike.

title: Craters of the Moon — Inferno Cone Climb Base
description: Inferno Cone is a short cinder climb with panoramic views of the Great Rift lava field. Spatter cones and tree molds nearby explain basaltic eruptions. Astronaut geology training lore adds Space Age color.

title: Sawtooth NRA — Redfish Lake Visitor Area
description: Redfish Lake sits under the Sawtooth Range's granite ramparts south of Stanley. Sockeye salmon once reddened the shores — hence the name. It is central Idaho's classic alpine lake basecamp.

title: Craters rim — Idaho — Menan Buttes Area
description: Menan Buttes are twin tuff cones on the Snake River Plain formed by explosive magma–water interaction. Trails climb the north butte for valley views. They are National Natural Landmarks of basaltic hydrovolcanism.

title: Grand Teton — Jenny Lake Visitor Area
description: Jenny Lake is a classic Teton glacial lake at the mouth of Cascade Canyon. Boat shuttles and trails lead toward Hidden Falls and Inspiration Point. Early climbers and dude ranches shaped valley culture.

title: Yellowstone — Mammoth Hot Springs Terraces
description: Mammoth's travertine terraces grow from limestone dissolved and redeposited by hot water — constantly changing staircases of white and orange. Fort Yellowstone's historic buildings nearby housed early Army park managers. Elk graze the parade grounds.

title: Yellowstone — West Thumb Geyser Basin
description: West Thumb's lakeshore geysers and hot springs sit on the edge of Yellowstone Lake within the caldera. Fishing Cone once tempted anglers to cook catches in the spring. Boardwalks protect fragile sinter.

title: Cody — Buffalo Bill Center of the West Area
description: The Buffalo Bill Center complex interprets Western art, Plains Indigenous cultures, firearms, and Buffalo Bill Cody's showman legacy. Cody town was founded by the scout and entertainer. Absaroka mountains frame the museum campus.

title: Thermopolis — Hot Springs State Park
description: Thermopolis claims the world's largest mineral hot spring, protected by a 1896 gift agreement involving the Eastern Shoshone and Northern Arapaho. Free bathhouse access continues that legacy. Rainbow terraces color the Bighorn River edge.

title: Guernsey — Oregon Trail Ruts State Historic Site
description: Sandstone at Guernsey holds some of the deepest Oregon Trail wagon ruts anywhere — cut by thousands of iron wheels. Register Cliff is nearby. The physical grooves make migration tangible.

title: Casper — National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
description: The Trails Center overlooks the North Platte where Oregon, California, Mormon, and Pony Express routes converged. Interactive exhibits simulate river crossings. Casper remains a crossroads of Plains travel.

title: Flaming Gorge — Red Canyon Overlook Visitor
description: Red Canyon Overlook frames Flaming Gorge Reservoir's turquoise water against vermilion cliffs. Ashley National Forest roads deliver rim views. John Wesley Powell's naming still fits at sunset.

title: Arches — Delicate Arch Viewpoint / Wolfe Ranch
description: Delicate Arch is Utah's freestanding icon above a slickrock bowl near Wolfe Ranch. The hike is a rite of passage; the distant viewpoint offers a non-summit angle. Evening light turns the Entrada sandstone neon.

title: Arches — Balanced Rock Pullout
description: Balanced Rock's precarious caprock atop a pedestal is an Arches roadside classic. Erosion will eventually topple it — as it did a nearby twin in 1975. Windows Section arches cluster just beyond.

title: Canyonlands — Grand View Point
description: Grand View Point surveys Island in the Sky's sheer drop to the Colorado–Green confluence country. White Rim roads thread far below. It is Canyonlands' signature mesa-edge panorama.

title: Bryce Canyon — Inspiration Point
description: Inspiration Point overlooks Bryce's amphitheater of hoodoos in Claron Formation limestone. Freeze-thaw and rain sculpt the pink cliffs into temples and fins. Paiute stories speak of Legend People turned to stone.

title: Zion — Canyon Overlook Trailhead
description: Canyon Overlook peers into lower Zion Canyon from the east side after the historic tunnel. Short trail, big reward over the switchbacks below. Navajo Sandstone cliffs glow at sunset.

title: Zion — Watchman Trailhead Area
description: The Watchman stands sentinel above Zion's south entrance and visitor center. Evening photography of the peak over the Virgin River is a park ritual. Southern Paiute homeland surrounds the canyon.

title: Grand Canyon — Mather Point
description: Mather Point is many visitors' first Grand Canyon gasp on the South Rim near the visitor center. Layered Paleozoic cliffs drop to the invisible Colorado. It is named for NPS founding leader Stephen Mather.

title: Grand Canyon — Hermits Rest
description: Mary Colter's Hermits Rest (1914) is a faux hermit hideaway at the end of Hermit Road with western canyon views. Hermit Trail descends toward the river. Shuttle-only seasons protect the rim.

title: Petrified Forest — Blue Mesa Scenic Road
description: Blue Mesa's bentonite badlands and petrified logs record Late Triassic rivers and conifers turned to quartz. Route 66 and early park history overlap the painted landscape. Crystal-filled wood still dazzles.

title: Petrified Forest — Painted Desert Inn
description: Painted Desert Inn is a CCC and Mary Colter–associated lodge overlooking pastel Chinle badlands. Murals by Hopi artist Fred Kabotie enrich the interior. It anchors the park's northern painted vistas.

title: Saguaro NP East — Broadway Trailhead Area
description: Saguaro National Park's Rincon Mountain district protects classic Sonoran Desert forests of towering saguaros. Broadway access leads into bajada trails at Tucson's edge. Bloom season crowns the giants with white flowers.

title: Saguaro NP West — Valley View Overlook Trail
description: Valley View frames dense saguaro stands against Tucson Mountains sunsets in the Tucson Mountain District. Signal Hill petroglyphs nearby speak to Hohokam presence. Urban-wildland contrast is striking.

title: Organ Mountains — Dripping Springs Natural Area
description: Dripping Springs sits beneath Organ Mountains granite needles with ruins of a sanatorium and resort. Trails lead toward the steep Organ Needles. It is Las Cruces' backyard sky island.

title: White Sands — Dune Life Nature Trail Area
description: Interdune trails interpret how plants and animals survive shifting gypsum. Trackways of kit foxes appear after calm nights. The brilliance of the dunes demands eye protection and water.

title: Great Sand Dunes — Zapata Falls Trailhead
description: Zapata Falls plunges through a narrow slot south of the dunes with Sangre de Cristo views. A short rocky walk reaches the amphitheater. It is a cool counterpoint to hot dune climbs.

title: Rocky Mountain NP — Bear Lake Trailhead
description: Bear Lake is a classic glacier-carved tarn at the end of Bear Lake Road with Hallett Peak reflecting in calm water. Trails radiate to Nymph, Dream, and Emerald lakes. Early arrival is required in peak season.

title: Rocky Mountain NP — Alpine Visitor Center
description: The Alpine Visitor Center sits near 11,800 feet on Trail Ridge Road — among the highest NPS visitor facilities. Tundra boardwalks demand respect for fragile plants. Elk browse valleys far below.

title: Colorado NM — Independence Monument View
description: Independence Monument is a freestanding Wingate tower John Otto climbed on July 4, 1911, to raise a flag. Rim views take in the Grand Valley. Otto's advocacy created the monument.

title: Black Canyon — Chasm View North Rim
description: Chasm View on the quieter North Rim peers into some of Black Canyon's narrowest, deepest sections. Painted Wall's light pegmatite dikes streak dark gneiss. Vertigo is part of the experience.

title: Curecanti — Morrow Point Overlook Area
description: Morrow Point Reservoir drowned a Gunnison River canyon segment beneath Curecanti National Recreation Area. Overlooks and boat tours interpret dam-era transformation. Blue Mesa nearby is Colorado's largest reservoir.

title: Great Basin — Lehman Caves Visitor Center
description: Lehman Caves' ornate limestone rooms were known to Indigenous peoples and later shown by rancher Absalom Lehman. Guided tours protect fragile formations. Wheeler Peak's alpine world rises immediately above.

title: Lake Tahoe — Emerald Bay Inspiration Point
description: Inspiration Point overlooks Emerald Bay, Fannette Island, and Vikingsholm — a Scandinavian-inspired mansion. Tahoe's clarity and depth are legendary. The bay is a California state park jewel.

title: Sequoia — Giant Forest Museum Area
description: Giant Forest holds the General Sherman Tree — the world's largest tree by volume — among sequoias that can exceed 2,000 years. Early park battles fought logging threats. Marble Fork drainages thread the grove.

title: Kings Canyon — Zumwalt Meadow Area
description: Zumwalt Meadow sits in a glaciated granite valley along the South Fork Kings River — often compared to Yosemite's quieter cousin. Cedar Grove access is seasonal. High Sierra peaks wall the canyon.

title: Pinnacles — High Peaks Trailhead Area
description: Pinnacles protects eroded remnants of an ancient volcano rafted north along the San Andreas. Condors soar over rock spires and talus caves. East and west entrances do not connect by park road.

title: Channel Islands — Ventura Harbor Mainland VC
description: Ventura Harbor is the primary mainland gateway to Channel Islands National Park's Fox Canyon foxes, sea caves, and marine sanctuary waters. Island fox recovery is a conservation win. Crossing the Santa Barbara Channel is the start of the adventure.

title: Joshua Tree — Arch Rock Nature Trail Area
description: Arch Rock is a short White Tank Campground walk to a granite arch in Mojave desert monzogranite. Boulders stacked by weathering define Joshua Tree's Wonderland of Rocks mood. Night skies here are outstanding.

title: Anza-Borrego — Fonts Point Overlook
description: Fonts Point overlooks Borrego Badlands' maze of eroded sediments in California's largest state park. Sunrise and sunset are prime; the sandy approach road prefers high clearance. Bighorn country surrounds the views.

title: Death Valley — Dante's View
description: Dante's View perches more than 5,000 feet above Badwater Basin for a map-like vista of Death Valley's extremes. Telescope Peak rises opposite across the trough. Temperature contrasts between rim and floor can be shocking.

title: Death Valley — Artists Palette Drive
description: Artists Palette's oxidized mineral colors streak volcanic hills along a one-way scenic loop. Soft evening light intensifies greens, pinks, and violets. It is geologic painting without a brush.

title: Manzanar National Historic Site
description: Manzanar interprets the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans in a desert camp beneath the Sierra. Reconstructed barracks and a cemetery monument demand reflection. It is a National Park Service site of conscience.

title: Golden Gate — Battery Spencer Overlook
description: Battery Spencer above the Golden Gate Bridge delivers the classic tower-and-city postcard view from the Marin Headlands. Endicott-era guns once guarded the entrance. Fog plays hide-and-seek with the span.

title: Point Reyes — Chimney Rock Trailhead
description: Chimney Rock's peninsula trail offers wildflowers, elephant seal views, and Pacific vistas near the lighthouse zone. Historic lifeboat station structures remain. It is Point Reyes' dramatic southern tip.

title: Red Rock Canyon State Park CA — Scenic Loop
description: Red Rock Canyon's dramatic cliffs along Highway 14 have starred in countless film shoots between Mojave and Walker Pass. Rainbow Basin–style colors meet Joshua trees. It is a quick geologic hit north of Los Angeles routes.

title: Valley of Fire — Mouse's Tank Trailhead
description: Mouse's Tank trail passes petroglyph panels to a natural rock basin that holds rainwater in the desert. Southern Paiute history layers the red sandstone. It is a short cultural and geologic walk.

title: Red Rock Canyon NCA — Scenic Drive Entrance
description: Red Rock Canyon's Keystone Thrust landscape rises west of Las Vegas with towering Aztec Sandstone. The 13-mile scenic drive samples pullouts and trailheads. It is a wild contrast to the Strip.

title: Great Basin Highway — Ward Charcoal Ovens
description: Ward Charcoal Ovens' beehive kilns produced charcoal for nearby silver smelters in the 1870s. The stone ovens remain remarkably intact in eastern Nevada. Starry skies here rank among the darkest.

title: Bryce — Natural Bridge Turnout
description: Natural Bridge is an arch carved in pink Claron limestone along Bryce's southern scenic drive. Despite the name, it is an arch formed by weathering rather than stream undercutting. Quiet compared to the main amphitheater.

title: Capitol Reef — Panorama Point & Goosenecks
description: Panorama Point surveys Waterpocket Fold country with a short spur to Sulphur Creek goosenecks. Capitol dome Navajo Sandstone forms appear along Highway 24. Orchards in Fruita remain a pioneer legacy.

title: Escalante — Head of the Rocks Overlook
description: Head of the Rocks on Scenic Byway 12 surveys slickrock domes of Grand Staircase–Escalante country. The ribbon of highway itself is an engineering and scenic marvel. Sunset colors run to the horizon.

title: Natural Bridges — Sipapu Bridge Viewpoint
description: Sipapu is the park's largest bridge, named with a Hopi term for the place of emergence. Loop roads link three bridges in White Canyon. Dark-sky park status makes nights extraordinary.

title: Hovenweep National Monument — Square Tower Group
description: Hovenweep's Square Tower Group preserves Ancestral Puebloan towers and rooms at canyon heads along the Utah–Colorado line. Precise masonry suggests astronomical and defensive functions. Quiet trails reward unhurried visits.

title: Canyon de Chelly — White House Overlook
description: White House Overlook views a cliff dwelling named for a long white-plastered wall in Canyon de Chelly. The trail down is sometimes open under Navajo Nation rules. Cottonwoods line the canyon floor farms.

title: Hubbell Trading Post National Historic Site
description: Hubbell Trading Post (1878) still operates on the Navajo Nation as the oldest continuously operating post of its kind in the NPS system. Rugs, jewelry, and cross-cultural trade stories fill the rooms. Ganado's cottonwoods shade the compound.

title: Walnut Canyon National Monument
description: Walnut Canyon's Sinagua cliff rooms line a forested limestone gorge east of Flagstaff. An island trail loops among dwellings with careful footing. It complements nearby Wupatki and Sunset Crater stories.

title: Montezuma Well Unit
description: Montezuma Well is a spring-fed limestone sinkhole with cliff dwellings and outlet canals used by Sinagua farmers. Unique aquatic species live in the constant-temperature water. It is a detached unit of Montezuma Castle NM.

title: Tonto National Monument Lower Cliff Dwelling
description: Tonto's cliff dwellings overlook Roosevelt Lake in the Superstition foothills, built by Salado peoples. Upper and lower ruins preserve adobe and masonry rooms. The drive via AZ-188 is a Desert Southwest classic.

title: Casa Grande Ruins National Monument
description: Casa Grande's great house is a multi-story Hohokam structure protected by a modern roof since early preservation efforts. Canal irrigation communities thrived in the Gila Valley. It is one of Arizona's oldest federal archaeological preserves.

title: Organ Pipe — Ajo Mountain Drive Start
description: Ajo Mountain Drive loops into organ pipe and saguaro habitat with desert washes and mountain backdrops. Borderland ecology includes senita cactus rare in the U.S. Summer heat demands dawn starts.

title: Chiricahua — Massai Point Overlook
description: Massai Point surveys balanced rocks and hoodoos of Chiricahua's rhyolite wonderland. Trails drop into Echo and Hailstone mazes. Sky Island biodiversity surrounds the stone city.

title: Coronado National Memorial — Montezuma Pass
description: Montezuma Pass overlooks the San Pedro Valley near the U.S.–Mexico line where Coronado's 1540 expedition entered present-day Arizona. Trails climb into the Huachucas. Borderland history is layered and contested.

title: Big Bend — Chisos Basin Visitor Center
description: Chisos Basin is a mountain island within Chihuahuan Desert, with the Window pour-off framing desert sunsets. Lodge and campground sit inside volcanic cliffs. It is Big Bend's cool high heart.

title: Big Bend — Fossil Discovery Exhibit Area
description: The Fossil Discovery Exhibit interprets giant pterosaurs and other Cretaceous fossils from Big Bend rocks. Roadside exhibits sit on the way to Persimmon Gap. The park's paleontology rivals its scenery.

title: Guadalupe Mountains — McKittrick Canyon Trailhead
description: McKittrick Canyon is famous for fall maple color in the Chihuahuan Desert and for Capitan reef geology. Pratt Cabin and the Grotto reward day hikers. Day-use gates protect the fragile canyon.

title: Carlsbad — Walnut Canyon Desert Drive Area
description: Walnut Canyon Desert Drive samples surface Chihuahuan Desert above the famous caves. Yucca and agave frame limestone hills. Evening bat flights launch from the natural entrance amphitheater nearby.

title: Hilo Liliʻuokalani Gardens
description: Japanese garden on Hilo Bay honoring Hawaiʻi's last monarch. Tsunami history reshaped the waterfront beyond the stone lanterns. Mauna Kea sometimes shows snow across the bay.

title: Huliheʻe Palace Grounds
description: Royal vacation palace on Aliʻi Drive in Kailua-Kona. Grounds interpret Hawaiian Kingdom social history beside Mokuaikaua Church. Oceanfront lawns face busy canoe waters.

title: Mokuaikaua Church
description: Oldest Christian church in Hawaiʻi (1837), built of lava rock and ʻōhiʻa. Missionary and Hawaiian congregation stories intertwine. It anchors Kailua Village's historic core.

title: Wailua Falls Kauaʻi Lookout
description: Roadside waterfall on Kauaʻi's east side once featured in television openings. Wailua River valley holds heiau and chiefly legends. Viewing pullouts fill quickly after rain when flow peaks.

title: Opaekaʻa Falls Lookout
description: Twin overlooks of Opaekaʻa Falls and the Wailua River. Signs cover canoe landings and sacred valley sites. Compact stop above Kapaʻa.

title: Koko Head Stairs Trailhead
description: Steep tramway-tie stairs climb a tuff cone to coastal bunkers and island views. Hanauma Bay and Kaiwi coast spill below. Little shade — carry water.

title: Papohaku Beach Park Molokaʻi
description: One of Hawaiʻi's longest white-sand beaches on Molokaʻi's west shore. Winter surf is often unsafe for swimming. Sunsets feel vast and lonely.

title: Hulopoʻe Beach Park Lānaʻi
description: Marine preserve beach near Manele Harbor with dolphins and tidepools. Ferry arrivals land next door. Coastal trail leads toward Puʻu Pehe.

title: Kalaupapa Overlook Palaʻau
description: Pali overlook of the Kalaupapa peninsula from Palaʻau State Park. Interpretive signs address the isolation settlement's history. Quiet respect fits the view.

title: Papakōlea Green Sand Approach
description: Olive-green olivine sand beach near South Point in a tuff cone amphitheater. Hike or authorized shuttle across windy pasture. One of few green sand beaches worldwide.

title: Wailua Falls Maui Pullout
description: Roadside falls on the Hāna Highway into a jungle pool. Streams drain Haleakalā's wet eastern slopes. Pull carefully — shoulder space is tight.

title: Puʻu Loa Petroglyphs
description: Thousands of petroglyphs on coastal pāhoehoe along Chain of Craters Road. Boardwalks protect the soft canvas. Motifs include human forms and paddles.

title: Beluga Point Turnagain Arm
description: Overlook of extreme tides and mudflats where belugas hunt. Cook named Turnagain Arm after having to turn back. Bore tides and mountain walls define the Seward Highway.

title: Independence Mine Hatcher Pass
description: Hard-rock gold mill ruins in alpine Hatcher Pass above Palmer. 1930s–50s mining built a high camp in the Talkeetnas. Boardwalks interpret the boom.

title: Worthington Glacier Wayside
description: Roadside glacier east of Thompson Pass on the Richardson Highway. Short trails reach blue ice views. Pass snowfall records are legendary.

title: Arctic Circle Dalton Wayside
description: Marks 66°33′N on the Trans-Alaska Pipeline haul road. Continuous daylight or darkness defines seasons. Reaching it is an Interior overlanding badge.

title: Hurricane Ridge VC
description: Most accessible Olympic alpine meadows and glacier views. Road climbs from Port Angeles into wind-scoured ridges. Classic rainshadow contrast.

title: Hoh Rain Forest VC
description: Temperate rainforest with well over 100 inches of rain yearly. Hall of Mosses drapes maples and spruce. One of the world's great remaining temperate rainforests.

title: Diablo Lake Overlook
description: Turquoise hydro reservoir colored by glacial flour on the North Cascades Highway. Dam history meets wilderness aesthetics. Peaks crowd the skyline.

title: Artist Point Mt Baker
description: End of Mount Baker Highway with Baker and Shuksan views. Snow often lingers into midsummer. Pacific Northwest postcard scenery.

title: Johnston Ridge Observatory
description: Faces the crater blasted open May 18, 1980. Named for volcanologist David Johnston. Pumice plains and downed forests remain vivid.

title: Palouse Falls SP
description: Falls carved by Ice Age Missoula Floods into basalt. Washington's official state waterfall. Channeled scablands geology in plain view.

title: Cape Disappointment Light Area
description: Mouth of the Columbia where Lewis and Clark reached the Pacific. Graveyard of the Pacific bar claimed many ships. Lighthouses and batteries guard the entrance.

title: Multnomah Falls Lodge
description: Oregon's tallest waterfall at 620 feet with 1925 lodge and Benson Bridge. Columbia River Basalt cliffs frame the plunge. Most visited Gorge cascade.

title: Cape Perpetua Lookout
description: 800-foot headland with CCC lookout heritage. Tidepools and Devil's Churn below. Oregon Coast public-lands highlight.

title: Crater Lake Rim Village
description: Caldera lake of Mount Mazama after eruption ~7,700 years ago. Clearest deep-blue water. Klamath traditions and science share the rim.

title: Smith Rock Misery Ridge TH
description: Welded tuff cliffs that helped birth American sport climbing. Crooked River bends below. Ranching history meets state park.

title: Painted Hills John Day
description: Colorful claystone bands from ancient floodplains and ash. Fossils rewrite Cenozoic mammal evolution. Protect fragile crusts on short trails.

title: Hells Canyon Overlook OR
description: Deepest river gorge in North America on the Snake. Nez Perce homeland and pioneer freight routes overlap. Ranch country drops into wild breaks.

title: Fort Rock Natural Area
description: Tuff ring in Oregon high desert; nearby cave yielded ancient footwear. Once stood in a pluvial lake. Northern Great Basin prehistory landmark.

title: Silver City ID Ghost Town Road
description: Owyhee Mountains silver boomtown with brick hotels and seasonal cabins. Remote BLM/forest roads still reach it. Classic Idaho ghost-town drive.

title: Craters of the Moon Loop
description: Great Rift lava field with cinder cones and tubes. Apollo astronauts trained here. Compact volcanic park on the Snake River Plain.

title: Mesa Falls Overlook
description: Henrys Fork plunges over rhyolite on Yellowstone Plateau flank. Rare unmodified large waterfall on a major Idaho river. CCC viewpoints.

title: City of Rocks Reserve
description: Granite domes guided California Trail emigrants; Register Rock graffiti remains. Premier climbing reserve. Silent City skyline of towers.

title: Glacier Point Yosemite
description: Overlook of Half Dome and valley floor from 3,200 feet above. Carriage-road spectacle since the 1800s. Ice-age granite sculpting on display.

title: Zabriskie Point
description: Badlands of ancient Furnace Creek lakebeds in golden waves. Named for a Borax executive; film-famous. Sunrise and sunset glow.

title: Badwater Basin
description: Lowest point in North America at 282 feet below sea level. Salt polygons from ephemeral lake evaporation. Explains Death Valley's name.

title: Keys View Joshua Tree
description: Overlook of Coachella Valley and San Andreas corridor. Peninsular Ranges on clear days. Situates the park in active tectonics.

title: Point Reyes Lighthouse
description: 1870 light on a foggy shipwreck tip. Steps to lantern room above elephant seals. Peninsula granite is an exotic terrane.

title: Morro Rock
description: 576-foot volcanic plug sacred to Chumash and a Spanish landmark. Quarry scars remain. Peregrines nest on cliffs.

title: Bixby Creek Bridge View
description: 1932 Art Deco arch that opened Big Sur to cars. Among California's most photographed coastal spans. Highway 1 icon.

title: Burney Falls
description: Wide waterfall fed by springs as well as surface flow. Roosevelt reportedly called it a wonder. Basalt and evergreens frame mist.

title: Ancient Bristlecone VC
description: Schulman Grove trees over 4,000 years old. Dendrochronology rewrote climate history. Thin White Mountains air shapes gnarled forms.

title: Mono Lake South Tufa
description: Tufa towers exposed as lake levels fell. Critical bird stop and water-politics landmark. Classic shoreline walk.

title: Valley of Fire Elephant Rock
description: Aztec Sandstone north of Las Vegas with petroglyphs and CCC picnic areas. Elephant Rock near east entrance. Mojave red-rock park.

title: Cathedral Gorge SP
description: Bentonite badlands into slots and spires near Panaca. CCC structures. Quiet eastern Nevada gem.

title: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive
description: Climbs toward bristlecones and Nevada's high peaks in Great Basin NP. Classic Basin and Range. Lehman Caves below.

title: Desert View Watchtower
description: Mary Colter's 1932 tower with eastern Grand Canyon vistas. Pueblo Revival architecture meets Painted Desert haze. South Rim east gate icon.

title: Spider Rock Overlook
description: 800-foot spire in Canyon de Chelly central to Diné Spider Woman stories. Cliff dwellings line walls. South Rim road access.

title: Sunset Crater Overlook
description: Erupted ~1085 CE, reshaping Sinagua settlement. Black cinders contrast painted desert. Loop links to Wupatki.

title: Wupatki Pueblo
description: Multi-story pueblo after Sunset Crater enriched soils. Pacific and Mesoamerican trade goods found. Between Flagstaff and Little Colorado.

title: Montezuma Castle NM
description: Sinagua cliff dwelling in a limestone alcove above Beaver Creek. Misnamed by settlers. Among Arizona's best-preserved sites.

title: Chiricahua Echo Canyon
description: Rhyolite hoodoos — Land of Standing-Up Rocks. Apache and Faraway Ranch history. Sky island trails.

title: Goosenecks SP Utah
description: Entrenched San Juan River meanders hundreds of feet below. Textbook Colorado Plateau viewpoint near Mexican Hat.

title: Natural Bridges Owachomo
description: Oldest thinnest of three stream-carved bridges under Cedar Mesa sandstone. Utah's first NPS unit. Ancestral Puebloan sites nearby.

title: Goblin Valley SP
description: Entrada hoodoos like a crowd of goblins. State park protects whimsical formations. Sandy maze for families and film crews.

title: Dead Horse Point SP
description: Overlook of Colorado River gooseneck near Canyonlands. Cowboy corral legend on the narrow peninsula. White Rim far below.

title: Golden Spike NHS
description: May 10, 1869 meeting of UP and CP rails at Promontory Summit. Replica engines recreate the ceremony. Desolate and consequential.

title: Trail Ridge Rock Cut
description: Highest continuous paved U.S. highway cresting above 12,000 feet. Alpine tundra feels Arctic. Ute and Arapaho high routes preceded cars.

title: Garden of the Gods Gateway
description: Vertical Fountain fins against Pikes Peak on Ute lands. Perkins family gifted free public access. Front Range icon.

title: Mesa Verde Chapin Mesa
description: Ancestral Puebloan cliff dwellings including Cliff Palace. Centuries of mesa farming before alcove move. Early U.S. archaeology landmark.

title: Great Sand Dunes VC Area
description: Tallest dunes in North America against the Sangres. Medano Creek surgelets fascinate each spring. Alpine–desert juxtaposition.

title: Black Canyon Gunnison Point
description: Sheer Precambrian gorge so narrow sunlight barely reaches the river. South Rim introduction. Among last Western canyons fully explored.

title: Colorado NM Grand View
description: John Otto's trailbuilding helped create red-rock canyons above Grand Junction. Rim Rock Drive. Independence Monument tower.

title: Dinosaur Quarry Exhibit
description: Carnegie Quarry wall of Morrison Formation bones left in place. 1909 discovery. Paleontology as architecture.

title: Devils Tower NM
description: Sacred columnar phonolite butte; first U.S. national monument (1906). Plains tribes' traditions continue. Climbing and cultural closures share the tower.

title: Mormon Row Barns
description: Homestead barns on sagebrush flats with Teton backdrop. 1890s Latter-day Saint settlers. Most photographed vernacular Rockies scene.

title: Old Faithful Education Center
description: Predictable eruptions helped create Yellowstone in 1872 — world's first national park. Boardwalks on a restless caldera. Iconic spout.

title: Grand Prismatic Overlook
description: Largest U.S. hot spring with rainbow microbial mats. Hill overlook shows full spectrum. Midway Geyser Basin masterpiece.

title: Artist Point Yellowstone
description: Lower Falls in the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. Hydrothermal colors. Moran paintings helped sell the park.

title: Lamar Valley Pullout
description: America's Serengeti for bison and wolf watching after 1990s reintroduction. Northern range glacial bottoms. Dawn and dusk prime.

title: Beartooth Pass Summit
description: Highway above 10,900 feet across alpine plateaus. Kuralt called it among America's most beautiful drives. Snow beside July pavement.

title: Logan Pass Glacier
description: Continental Divide apex of Going-to-the-Sun Road (1932). Hidden Lake and goats. Glacier retreat visible nearby.

title: Many Glacier Hotel
description: 1915 Swiss-chalet lodge by Great Northern Railway. Swiftcurrent Lake mirrors peaks. America's Alps marketing made real.

title: Pompeys Pillar NM
description: William Clark's 1806 signature — only remaining physical Lewis and Clark evidence on-route. Yellowstone River bluff. Older petroglyphs too.

title: Little Bighorn Battlefield
